definition_zh: 曲调动听的；音调优美的；悦耳的
definition_en: pleasant to listen to because the notes follow a clear and agreeable melody
core_image: 窗边有人轻轻哼着一段好听的调子，音符一个接一个顺顺地落下来
scene: 傍晚的巷子里，老人抱着一把旧吉他拨出旋律，路过的人都放慢脚步，说这声音真好听。In the evening alley, an old man plucked a melody on a worn guitar, and passing neighbours slowed down to hear such a tuneful sound.
sceneCN: 这里 tuneful 是「悦耳的」（第 1 个义项：旋律动听、听着舒服）；句意：傍晚巷子里老人拨出旋律，路过的人放慢脚步，觉得那声音真好听。

pos.zh: 曲调动听的；音调优美的

derivatives.zh: 悦耳；曲调动听，由 tuneful 加表示性质的名词词尾构成
悦耳地；音调优美地，由 tuneful 加副词词尾构成
曲调；调子，tuneful 的词根名词
不成调的；五音不全的，加否定词尾构成的反义词

senses.title: Pleasant because of a clear melody
senses.definition: having a tune that is easy to follow and nice to hear
senses.definitionCN: 带有清晰、容易跟唱而且悦耳的旋律
senses.example: The trio sang a tuneful folk song at the village party.
senses.exampleCN: 三人在村里的聚会上唱了一首悦耳的民歌。
senses.why: Tuneful adds the ending that means full of to tune, so anything full of a good tune sounds pleasant.
senses.whyCN: tuneful 在 tune 后加上表示「充满……」的形容词词尾，所以「充满好曲调」的东西听起来就舒服，这就是最直接的义项。

senses.title: Said of a voice that stays in key
senses.definition: describing a singer whose notes are accurate and musical
senses.definitionCN: 形容歌唱者音准好、听起来有乐感
senses.example: Her tuneful alto carried easily over the noise of the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 她那悦耳的女低音很轻松地盖过了人群的喧闹。
senses.why: Since tune also means being in pitch, the adjective naturally describes people who sing on key.
senses.whyCN: tune 还表示「音准」，所以这个形容词自然用来描述唱得准、唱得好的嗓音，从「有曲调」扩展到「把音唱对」。

senses.title: Easy to remember, like a catchy air
senses.definition: describing music or words that follow a simple pattern you can hum or repeat
senses.definitionCN: 形容音乐或词句有简单好记的模式，可以随口哼唱或复述
senses.example: The advert uses a tuneful jingle that stays in your head.
senses.exampleCN: 这则广告用了一段朗朗上口的铃声，让人念念不忘。
senses.why: A tune is something you carry away by humming, so tuneful stretches from pleasant to memorable.
senses.whyCN: 曲调是能带回家哼出来的东西，所以从「好听」进一步引申为「好记、容易复用」，广告与流行歌最常这样用。

intro.en: Tuneful is tune plus the ending -ful. Tune itself came through French from a word for tone, and English first used it for a tone or sound before it meant a melody.
intro.cn: tuneful 由 tune 加 -ful 构成。tune 经法语来自表示「音调」的词，英语早期先用它表示调子与声音，后来才特指旋律。

items.en: Greek tonos means a stretching, then a pitch or accent of voice.
items.cn: 希腊语 tonos 本义是「绷紧」，引申为嗓音的高低与重音。

items.en: Latin tonus takes the Greek word for tone or pitch.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tonus 承接希腊语中表示音调、音高的词。

items.en: Old French ton carries the sense of a sound or a tone of voice.
items.cn: 古法语 ton 保留了「声音、语调」这一类含义。

items.en: English tune first means a tone or a sound, and later a melody.
items.cn: 英语中古期的 tune 先指音调、声响，随后才转向旋律。

items.en: Tuneful, full of tune, appears once tune clearly means a melody.
items.cn: 当 tune 明确表示「曲调」之后，tuneful 这一写法才开始流行，意为「充满曲调的」。

items.en: Modern English applies tuneful to songs, voices, birds and even speech.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词用于歌曲、嗓音、鸟鸣，甚至说话的声音。

note.en: Tuneful is close to its own word family and to other words that judge sound as pleasant.
note.cn: tuneful 与它自己的词族关系紧密，又与评价声音是否悦耳的单词同处一片语义圈。

entries.definition: without a clear tune, or singing badly
entries.definitionCN: 不成调的；唱歌走音的，由同一词根加否定词尾构成

entries.definition: a sequence of notes that forms a melody
entries.definitionCN: 曲调，是 tuneful 的词根名词

entries.definition: happening at a suitable moment
entries.definitionCN: 及时的；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: producing a sweet, flowing series of notes
entries.definitionCN: 旋律婉转的，比 tuneful 更书面

entries.definition: easy to remember and keep humming
entries.definitionCN: 容易上口、好记的，偏口语

entries.definition: related to pleasant combinations of musical notes
entries.definitionCN: 和谐的，侧重音与音的配合

normalIntro.en: Tuneful is tune plus the ending -ful, meaning full of a tune, so the word simply says this sound has a good tune inside it.
normalIntro.cn: tuneful 是 tune 加词尾 -ful（充满……的），字面就是「充满曲调」，所以这个词直接说某声音里有个好调子。

normal.en: The ending -ful means full of, so tuneful means full of tune.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ful 表示充满，所以 tuneful 就是充满曲调。

normal.en: The opposite tunes is not a word, but tuneless is: it means without any tune.
normal.cn: 反义词不是 tunes，而是 tuneless，意为没有调子。

normal.en: Compare tuneful and tuneless: one full of melody, one stripped of it.
normal.cn: 对比 tuneful 与 tuneless：一个有旋律，一个没旋律。

normal.en: It usually sits before a noun: a tuneful song, a tuneful whistle.
normal.cn: 它通常放在名词前：a tuneful song、a tuneful whistle。

normal.en: For comparison use more tuneful, not tune fuller.
normal.cn: 比较级用 more tuneful，不能写成 tune fuller。

abstract.en: See small notes falling one after another like a string of beads.
abstract.cn: 想象音符像一串珠子，一个接一个顺顺地落下来。

abstract.en: Hear a bird repeating the same short phrase in the morning.
abstract.cn: 想象清晨一只鸟反复唱着同样的小段。

abstract.en: Picture a jingle you hum without noticing an hour later.
abstract.cn: 想象一段广告铃声，一小时后你不知不觉就哼起来了。

examples.en: The choir gave a tuneful performance that pleased the whole audience.
examples.cn: 合唱团献上了一场悦耳的演出，全场观众都很满意。

examples.en: Her new album is more tuneful than her earlier ones.
examples.cn: 她的新专辑比前几张更好听。

examples.en: Even the traffic outside could not spoil his tuneful mood.
examples.cn: 就连外面的车流也破坏不了他哼着调子的好心情。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「囤福」——囤着一曲好调子像囤着一份福气，听着心里舒服，就是悦耳动听。这只是拆音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 tonos（绷紧→音高）→ 拉丁语 tonus → 古法语 ton → 英语 tune（音调；曲调）+ 英语词尾 -ful（充满……的）→ tuneful 悦耳的，核心义「充满好曲调」。

sensesIntro.en: Tuneful starts from a melody that pleases, moves to a voice that keeps in key, and ends as a catchy pattern you can recall.
sensesIntro.cn: tuneful 先从动听的旋律出发，转到音准好的嗓音，最后指朗朗上口、容易被记住的调子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a humming voice that follows a clear, happy line of notes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条清晰明快的音符线被轻声哼出来。

branches.en: A clear melody is the central sense.
branches.cn: 清晰的旋律是核心义项。

branches.en: A mouth that sings on key extends the same idea to people.
branches.cn: 唱得准的嗓音，把同一个意思延伸到人身上。

branches.en: A tune you can carry away makes the catchy sense.
branches.cn: 能被带走、随口哼出的调子，形成好记的义项。

branches.en: A song is called tuneful when both the melody and the singer hold up.
branches.cn: 旋律与歌者都立得住时，一首歌才被称作悦耳。

branches.en: Pleasant and memorable come from the same simple shape of notes.
branches.cn: 好听与好记，出自同一个简单顺耳的音形。

intro.en: Tuneful pairs a French and Latin root with a very productive English ending.
intro.cn: tuneful 把一个来自法语与拉丁语的词根，与一个构词能力极强的英语词尾组合起来。

latinIntro.en: Latin tonus, from Greek tonos, gives the tone behind tune.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tonus（源自希腊语 tonos）提供了 tune 背后的「音调」义。

items.example: She knows every tune in the show.
items.exampleCN: 剧中每段曲调她都熟悉。

items.example: The ending -ful forms joyful and hopeful.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ful 可构成 joyful 与 hopeful。

items.example: The tuneful refrain closes the song.
items.exampleCN: 悦耳的副歌给这首歌收尾。

items.example: The ending -less forms tuneless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 tuneless。

items.example: Tuneless humming drifted from the corridor.
items.exampleCN: 走廊里飘着走调的哼唱。

items.example: The ending -ness forms tunefulness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 tunefulness。

items.example: The ending -ly forms tunefully.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 tunefully。

items.example: The workers sang tunefully while digging.
items.exampleCN: 工人们一边挖土一边悦耳地哼唱。

items.example: Greek tonos begins the chain to tune.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语 tonos 是通到 tune 的起点。

items.example: Latin tonus carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 tonus 把这词带进了法语。

definition_zh: 浑浊的；污浊的；含沙的；含糊不清的
definition_en: having liquid that is thick, muddy, or clouded with solid matter
core_image: 搅动后的河水：泥沙翻起，水变得看不清底
scene: 暴雨过后，河水被泥沙搅得发黄，根本看不见水底的石头。After the rainstorm, the river ran turbid and hid the stones on its bed.
sceneCN: 这里 turbid 是「浑浊的」（第 1 个义项：液体因悬浮物而看不清）；句意：暴雨过后，河水被泥沙搅得发黄，根本看不见水底的石头。

derivatives.zh: 基础词加后缀 -ity 构成，指「浑浊度；污浊」
基础词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，指「浑浊地；含糊地」
基础词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，指「浑浊的状态」
turbid 加计量词尾 -meter 构成，指测量浑浊度的仪器

senses.title: Clouded with suspended matter
senses.definition: thick and cloudy with stirred up mud, silt, or dirt
senses.definitionCN: 因泥、沙或污物被搅起而变浓、变得看不清
senses.example: The flood left the stream turbid for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后，这条小溪好几个星期都很浑浊。
senses.why: The Latin root means a crowd in disorder, so the first picture is many particles churning together in water.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「混乱的人群」，因此最初画面是许多颗粒在水里一起翻搅。

senses.title: A full load of sediment
senses.titleCN: 含沙量高的；泥沙翻滚的
senses.definition: carrying so much sand or silt that the water cannot be seen through
senses.definitionCN: 携带大量沙子或淤泥，水完全无法透见
senses.example: Sediment samples were taken from the turbid river mouth.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员在含沙量高的河口采集了泥沙样本。
senses.why: The disorder of the crowd becomes visible as a load of solid grains spread through the whole body of water.
senses.whyCN: 人群的混乱具体化为大量颗粒分布在整个水体中，于是有了含沙量高的义项。

senses.title: Muddy and unhealthy
senses.definition: referring to a body fluid that looks unclear or unhealthy
senses.definitionCN: 指体液外观不清、带有病态浑浊
senses.example: The doctor noted turbid fluid in the sample.
senses.exampleCN: 医生注意到样本中有浑浊的液体。
senses.why: Any liquid that no longer looks clear repeats the image of stirred up matter, so doctors borrow the word for body fluids.
senses.whyCN: 任何不再清澈的液体都会重现「被搅起杂物」的画面，所以医生也借用这个词描述体液。

senses.title: Muddled in style or thought
senses.definition: overcrowded and unclear, as of wording or reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 文辞或思路因堆砌混乱而含义不清
senses.example: His essay was admired for its passion but faulted for its turbid style.
senses.exampleCN: 他的文章因热情受到赞赏，却因文风晦涩而受批评。
senses.why: A lot of material packed together without order turns clear water cloudy, and an overloaded sentence turns clear thought cloudy too.
senses.whyCN: 材料大量堆砌而缺乏条理，会让清水变浊；句子塞得太满，思路也随之一片模糊。

senses.title: Impenetrable to view
senses.definition: so clouded that nothing behind it can be made out
senses.definitionCN: 浑浊到后面什么都分辨不清
senses.example: The divers waited until the turbid water cleared.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水员一直等到浑浊的水变清澈才下水。
senses.why: Loss of transparency is the common thread of every sense: what was see-through becomes a wall of stirred particles.
senses.whyCN: 失去透明是各义项的共同线索：原本透光的东西变成了一道由翻搅颗粒构成的墙。

intro.en: Turbid comes from Latin turbidus, muddy or confused, from turba, a crowd in disorder, from turba in the sense of a disturbance.
intro.cn: turbid 来自拉丁语 turbidus（浑浊的、混乱的），源于 turba（混乱的人群），再与「搅动、骚动」的意象相连。

items.en: Turba names a crowd or a disturbance.
items.cn: turba 指人群或骚动。

items.en: Turbare means to stir up or throw into confusion.
items.cn: turbare 意为搅动、使混乱。

items.en: Turbidus describes water made unclear or a mind in disorder.
items.cn: turbidus 描述变浊的水或混乱的心绪。

items.en: English borrows turbid from French and Latin learned usage.
items.cn: 英语经法语与拉丁学术用法借入 turbid。

items.en: The word settles into scientific and literary use for unclear liquid and unclear prose.
items.cn: 该词在现代英语中稳定用于科学描述浑浊液体，也用于文学批评中的晦涩文风。

note.en: Turbid is the adjective of stirred and clouded liquid, close to its Latin family and to words for dirty water.
note.cn: turbid 是描述被搅动、变浊液体的形容词，与拉丁同族词以及「脏水」类词相邻。

entries.definition: a state of violent disorder in air or water
entries.definitionCN: 气流或水流剧烈紊乱的状态

entries.definition: violent and disordered
entries.definitionCN: 动荡的；紊乱的

entries.definition: to interrupt or upset
entries.definitionCN: 打扰；搅乱

entries.definition: full of mud and not clear
entries.definitionCN: 泥泞的；浑浊的

entries.definition: dark and hard to see through
entries.definitionCN: 昏暗的；浑浊的（尤指水体）

entries.definition: not transparent
entries.definitionCN: 多云的；不清澈的

normalIntro.en: Turbid is the adjective of stirred water: a crowd of particles stands between you and the bottom.
normalIntro.cn: turbid 是「被搅动的水」的形容词：一群颗粒挡在你和河底之间。

normal.en: Turbid water looks like stirred mud.
normal.cn: turbid water 看上去就像被搅乱的泥浆。

normal.en: The turbid river carries a heavy load of silt.
normal.cn: turbid river 指含沙量很大的河流。

normal.en: Turbidity is the noun for the cloudy state.
normal.cn: turbidity 是表示「浑浊度」的名词。

normal.en: Compare the root in disturb: both involve stirring something up.
normal.cn: 对比 disturb 里的同一词根：两者都有「搅动」之意。

normal.en: Muddy and murky are plainer everyday words for turbid.
normal.cn: muddy 与 murky 是 turbid 的日常同义词。

abstract.en: Picture a clear pool turned gray the moment a stick stirs up the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一根棍子搅动池底，清水瞬间变成灰色。

abstract.en: Imagine a jar of sand and water shaken until you see nothing but haze.
abstract.cn: 想象一瓶沙水被摇个不停，最后只看得到一片雾。

abstract.en: Think of a test tube of liquid with a gray cloud in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一支试管里有一团灰色云雾。

examples.en: The flood left the river turbid for several days.
examples.cn: 洪水过后，河水浑浊了好几天。

examples.en: Farmers worried about the turbid water in the irrigation ditch.
examples.cn: 农民担心灌溉渠里浑浊的水。

examples.en: Turbidity is measured by how much light the water lets through.
examples.cn: 水的浑浊度通过它能让多少光透过来衡量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特必得」——水一旦被搅得「特」浑浊，「必」然看「得」见泥沙在翻；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 turba（混乱的人群）→ turbare（搅动、使混乱）→ turbidus（浑浊的）→ 拉丁/法语 → 英语 turbid，核心义「被搅得看不清」。

sensesIntro.en: Turbid begins with water clouded by stirred particles, then extends to sediment loaded water, medical fluids, muddled style, and any surface too clouded to see through.
sensesIntro.cn: turbid 先指被搅起颗粒而变浊的水，再扩展到含沙量高的水流、医学上的体液、晦涩的文风，以及任何看不透的表面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stirred river where mud hides the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：被搅动后泥沙遮住河底的河水。

branches.en: Clouded liquid is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 浑浊的液体是基本义项。

branches.en: Sediment loaded water is the physical extension.
branches.cn: 含沙量高的水流是物理层面的延伸。

branches.en: Medical use applies the same look to body fluids.
branches.cn: 医学用法把同样外观用于体液。

branches.en: Muddled prose repeats the disorder in thought.
branches.cn: 晦涩的文风把混乱搬到了思维层面。

branches.en: Opacity is the shared feature of both water and air.
branches.cn: 看不透是水体与空气共有的特征。

intro.en: Turbid is built on the Latin turba root and grows into turbidity, turbidly and turbidimeter.
intro.cn: turbid 以拉丁语 turba 词根为基础，衍生出 turbidity、turbidly 与 turbidimeter。

latinIntro.en: Latin turba means a crowd, and turbidus means muddy or confused.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 turba 意为人群，turbidus 意为浑浊的或混乱的。

items.example: Turba supplies the idea of a confused mass.
items.exampleCN: turba 提供「成群混乱」的意象。

items.example: Turbare is the act of stirring water or a crowd.
items.exampleCN: turbare 是把水或人群搅乱的动作。

items.example: Turbidus is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: turbidus 是直接来源。

items.example: Turbid keeps the muddy sense.
items.exampleCN: turbid 保留「浑浊」含义。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ity forms turbidity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 turbidity。

items.example: Turbidity is measured in the lab.
items.exampleCN: 浑浊度在实验室里测量。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms turbidly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 turbidly。

items.example: The element -meter forms turbidimeter.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 -meter 构成 turbidimeter。

items.example: A turbidimeter checks water quality.
items.exampleCN: 浑浊度计用于检查水质。

definition_zh: 塔楼；角楼；（坦克、军舰上的）炮塔；（战车上的）小塔
definition_en: a small tower, often attached to a larger building or set on a wall, or a similar rotating structure that carries a gun
core_image: 城堡墙角探出的小塔：高过墙头，四面开着窄窗
scene: 城堡的墙角伸出一座小塔，守军可以从上面看到整片山谷。At the corner of the castle wall, a turret rose above the battlements and offered a view of the whole valley.
sceneCN: 这里 turret 是「塔楼；角楼」（第 1 个义项：附在建筑或城墙上的小塔）；句意：城堡的墙角伸出一座小塔，守军可以从上面看到整片山谷。

derivatives.zh: 基础词加后缀 -ed 构成，形容建筑「有角楼的、带塔的」
基础词加后缀 -less 构成，形容车辆「无炮塔的」

senses.title: A small tower on a building
senses.definition: a small tower that stands out from a larger building, often at a corner
senses.definitionCN: 从较大建筑中伸出的小塔，常位于转角处
senses.example: The old church has a round turret on the west side.
senses.exampleCN: 这座古老教堂的西侧有一座圆形塔楼。
senses.why: The Italian diminutive turretta means a little tower, so the first picture is a tower shrunk down to a decorative corner.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语指小形式 turretta 意为「小塔」，所以最初画面是缩成装饰性墙角的小塔。

senses.title: A projecting defensive tower
senses.definition: a tower that juts out from a castle wall so defenders can fire along the wall
senses.definitionCN: 从城墙向外凸出的小塔，守军可沿墙射击
senses.example: Guards watched the gate from the turret above it.
senses.exampleCN: 守卫从门上的凸出塔楼监视大门。
senses.why: Cantilevered out from the wall, a turret gave sight and shots that a flat wall could not.
senses.whyCN: 从墙面悬挑出来的塔楼提供了平墙给不了的视野和火力。

senses.title: A rotating gun housing
senses.definition: an enclosed, often revolving mount that holds a cannon or guns
senses.definitionCN: 封闭且常可旋转的装置，用于安装火炮或机枪
senses.example: The tank turned its turret to face the road.
senses.exampleCN: 坦克转动炮塔，对准了那条路。
senses.why: A gun house keeps the vertical tower shape but sits on a ring, so it can turn like a head.
senses.whyCN: 炮房保留了垂直塔状外形，只是装在圆环上，于是能像头部一样转动。

senses.title: A little tower on a vehicle
senses.definition: a tower-like structure fixed on a war vehicle or engine of war
senses.definitionCN: 固定在战车或攻城器械上的塔状结构
senses.example: The old siege engine carried an armoured turret of wood.
senses.exampleCN: 那架老式攻城器械上带着一个木制的小塔。
senses.why: Early siege machines were rolling walls, so builders fixed small towers on them just as they did on stone walls.
senses.whyCN: 早期攻城器械就是会行走的城墙，于是工匠把石墙上那样的小塔也装了上去。

senses.title: A tower for the eye
senses.definition: any raised structure that lets one look out over a place
senses.definitionCN: 任何能让人俯瞰一地的高处结构
senses.example: A small turret of glass holds the lighthouse lamp.
senses.exampleCN: 灯塔的灯装在一个玻璃小塔里。
senses.why: Once a turret means a raised point for looking out, any small high structure that gives a view can borrow the word.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 turret 表示「用来眺望的高处」，任何提供视野的小型高结构都可以借用这个词。

intro.en: Turret comes from Old French touret, a diminutive of tour, tower, ultimately from Latin turris, with the same root behind tower.
intro.cn: turret 来自古法语 touret，是 tour（塔）的指小形式，更早可追溯至拉丁语 turris，与英语 tower 同源。

items.en: Turris means a tower or a fortress.
items.cn: turris 意为塔或堡垒。

items.en: Tour means a tower, and touret a small one.
items.cn: tour 意为塔，touret 意为小塔。

items.en: Touret enters English as turet in military building accounts.
items.cn: touret 在军事营建记录中以 turet 的形式进入英语。

items.en: Turret names the small tower that projects from a castle wall.
items.cn: 中古英语 turret 指从城墙上凸出的小塔。

items.en: Naval and armoured vehicles give the word a rotating gun housing.
items.cn: 舰船与装甲车辆使该词新增「可旋转炮塔」一义。

note.en: Turret is the small-tower noun of the tower family, and it also stands beside the terms for castle and gun structures.
note.cn: turret 是「塔」词族里的小塔名词，同时也与城堡和火炮结构这类词相邻。

entries.definition: a tall narrow building or structure
entries.definitionCN: 塔；高楼

entries.definition: the Old French form meaning a small tower
entries.definitionCN: 古法语词形，意为小塔

entries.definition: having a turret or turrets
entries.definitionCN: 带塔楼的；有角楼的

entries.definition: a strong part of a fortification that juts out
entries.definitionCN: 棱堡；堡垒的凸出部分

entries.definition: a small dome rising from a roof
entries.definitionCN: 穹顶塔楼；小圆顶

entries.definition: the rotating structure that holds a gun
entries.definitionCN: 炮架；火炮安装座

normalIntro.en: Turret is a tower shrunk to a small round cap on top of a corner.
normalIntro.cn: turret 就是缩小成一个圆形小帽、扣在墙角的塔。

normal.en: A turret is a little tower, from the French diminutive.
normal.cn: turret 是小塔，来自法语的指小形式。

normal.en: Every castle corner seems to end in a turret.
normal.cn: 城堡的每个转角似乎都以一座小塔收尾。

normal.en: A gun turret turns like a head on a neck.
normal.cn: gun turret 的转动就像脖子上的头。

normal.en: Turrets are much smaller than the main tower.
normal.cn: turret 比主塔小得多。

normal.en: The word shares its origin with tower.
normal.cn: 这个词与 tower 同源。

abstract.en: Picture a mushroom growing at the corner of a stone wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一朵蘑菇长在石墙的转角上。

abstract.en: Imagine two round caps pushing out from the two front corners of a fortress.
abstract.cn: 想象堡垒前墙的两个角向上各撑出一顶圆帽。

abstract.en: Think of a small armored head that can swing around to look in any direction.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小小的装甲头部，可以随意转过来朝任何方向看。

examples.en: The castle turret offered a clear view of the valley.
examples.cn: 城堡的塔楼提供了俯瞰山谷的开阔视野。

examples.en: The warship mounted four heavy guns in one forward turret.
examples.cn: 这艘军舰在前部的一座炮塔里装了四门重炮。

examples.en: A row of turrets lines the outer wall of the old fortress.
examples.cn: 一排塔楼沿着古老堡垒的外墙排开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「他瑞特」——「他」站在城堡小「塔」里，视野「特」别好；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 turris（塔）→ 古法语 tour（塔）→ 指小形式 touret（小塔）→ 中古英语 turet/turret，核心义「大墙上的小塔」。

sensesIntro.en: Turret starts as a little tower, extends to the projecting watchtower and the rotating gun housing, and ends with war vehicles and any raised lookout.
sensesIntro.cn: turret 先指小塔，再扩展到凸出的防御塔楼与可旋转炮塔，最后落到战车上的小塔以及泛指的高处观察点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round little tower jutting out of a castle corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：从城堡墙角伸出的小圆塔。

branches.en: A decorative small tower is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 装饰性的小塔是基本义项。

branches.en: A projecting tower is the military extension.
branches.cn: 凸出的塔楼是军事上的延伸。

branches.en: An armored revolving housing keeps the protecting shape.
branches.cn: 装甲可旋转炮房保留了「保护性外壳」的形状。

branches.en: A tower on a war vehicle moves the image onto a machine.
branches.cn: 战车上的小塔把这一形象搬到了器械上。

branches.en: Any raised lookout repeats the seeing-from-above idea.
branches.cn: 任何高处观察点都重复了「从上面看」的观念。

intro.en: Turret is the diminutive of the tower word, and English adds -ed and -less to it.
intro.cn: turret 是「塔」一词的指小形式，英语又在其上加了 -ed 与 -less。

latinIntro.en: Latin turris gives tower and turret alike, and Old French touret shrinks it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 turris 同时产生 tower 与 turret，古法语 touret 把它缩小。

items.example: Turris is the ultimate source of the family.
items.exampleCN: turris 是整个词族的最早来源。

items.example: Tour comes from Latin turris.
items.exampleCN: tour 来自拉丁语 turris。

items.example: The suffix -et forms touret.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -et 构成 touret。

items.example: Touret is borrowed directly into English.
items.exampleCN: touret 被直接借入英语。

items.example: Turret keeps both the tower and gun senses.
items.exampleCN: turret 兼有塔楼与炮塔两义。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms turreted.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 turreted。

items.example: Turreted describes a castle outline.
items.exampleCN: turreted 描述城堡轮廓。

items.example: The suffix -less forms turretless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 turretless。

items.example: Turretless describes some armoured vehicles.
items.exampleCN: turretless 形容某些装甲车辆。

definition_zh: 龟；海龟；龟肉；（比喻）翻个底朝天
definition_en: a reptile with a hard shell that lives on land or in water, or the act of turning upside down
core_image: 龟背上厚实的硬壳，遇到危险就把头缩进去
scene: 海边沙滩上，一只小龟拖着湿漉漉的壳朝浪里爬去。On the sandy beach, a small turtle dragged its wet shell toward the waves.
sceneCN: 这里 turtle 是「龟」（第 1 个义项：带硬壳的爬行动物）；句意：海边沙滩上，一只小龟拖着湿漉漉的壳朝浪里爬去。

derivatives.zh: 基础词加后缀 -ing 构成，指「捕龟；翻龟的身」（航海旧用法）
turtle 与 back 复合而成，指「龟背状的隆起」
turtle 与 neck 复合而成，指「高领毛衣」

senses.title: A shelled reptile
senses.definition: a slow reptile whose body is protected by a hard shell
senses.definitionCN: 一种行动缓慢、身体由硬壳保护的爬行动物
senses.example: A turtle laid her eggs in the warm sand.
senses.exampleCN: 一只海龟把蛋产在温暖的沙子里。
senses.why: The French tortue took on English spelling through the sound of a bird, and the animal keeps the core picture of a moving shell.
senses.whyCN: 法语 tortue 借英语时受「斑鸠」一词读音影响而拼作 turtle，动物本身保留了「会走动的壳」这一核心画面。

senses.title: The meat of the animal
senses.definition: the flesh of a turtle used as food
senses.definitionCN: 作为食物使用的龟的肉
senses.example: Turtle soup was once a costly dish on sailing ships.
senses.exampleCN: 龟汤过去在帆船上是一道昂贵的菜。
senses.why: In old cookbooks the animal name simply shifts from the creature to what is served on the plate.
senses.whyCN: 在旧式食谱里，动物名直接从「这种动物」转到「端上桌的食物」。

senses.title: Turning upside down
senses.definition: to overturn or capsize, especially of a boat
senses.definitionCN: 翻转或倾覆，尤指船只
senses.example: The rowing boat turtled in the sudden squall.
senses.exampleCN: 划子在那场突来的狂风里翻了。
senses.why: A turtle on its back cannot right itself, and sailors saw the same helplessness in a capsized hull.
senses.whyCN: 龟四脚朝天就翻不回来，水手在倾覆的船体上也看到了同样的无助。

senses.title: A slow and safe mover
senses.definition: someone or something that moves defensively and at a gentle pace
senses.definitionCN: 行事保守、速度平缓的人或事物
senses.example: Our bus is a turtle, but it never misses a stop.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的公交车慢得像龟，却从不错过一站。
senses.why: The shell suggests protection and the slow crawl suggests caution, so the word becomes a mild label for cautious slowness.
senses.whyCN: 壳暗示保护，缓慢爬行暗示谨慎，于是这个词逐渐成为对「稳健而缓慢」的温和称谓。

senses.title: A high rolled collar
senses.definition: a close fitting rolled collar on a sweater
senses.definitionCN: 毛衣上紧贴脖颈的翻折领口
senses.example: She pulled the turtle neck over her chin.
senses.exampleCN: 她把高领拉到下巴。
senses.why: A rolled sweater collar looks like a turtle pulling its neck into its shell, so the animal name moves into clothing.
senses.whyCN: 卷起的毛衣领口像龟把头缩进壳里，于是动物名进入了服装领域。

intro.en: Turtle comes from French tortue, which English altered under influence of turtledove, a long standing alteration of a borrowing.
intro.cn: turtle 来自法语 tortue，英语在「斑鸠」turtledove 一词影响下改动了拼写，属于借词受到同形音词牵引的典型例子。

items.en: Late Latin tortuca names a turtle or tortoise.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 tortuca 指龟或陆龟。

items.en: Tortue carries the word into French.
items.cn: tortue 把这个词带入法语。

items.en: English borrows tortue and reshapes it as turtle, echoing turtledove.
items.cn: 英语借入 tortue，并受 turtledove（斑鸠）影响改成 turtle。

items.en: Turtle first covers sea turtles and freshwater ones, while tortoise stays for land species.
items.cn: 现代英语中 turtle 主要指海龟与淡水龟，陆龟另用 tortoise。

items.en: Nautical use gives the compound turn turtle for capsizing.
items.cn: 航海用法产生了短语 turn turtle，表示翻船。

note.en: Turtle is the sea and fresh water member of the shelled reptile family, and the phrase turn turtle carries its upside down image into sailing.
note.cn: turtle 是龟鳖类中偏海生与淡水的一员，turn turtle 这一短语又把「四脚朝天」的画面带进了航海。

entries.definition: a slow land reptile with a shell
entries.definitionCN: 陆龟（与 turtle 同源于 tortue）

entries.definition: a kind of small wild dove
entries.definitionCN: 斑鸠（只是读音影响了 turtle 的拼写，与龟并非同源）

entries.definition: a small turtle that lives in fresh or brackish water
entries.definitionCN: 淡水或半咸水中的小型龟

entries.definition: the land dwelling shelled reptile
entries.definitionCN: 陆生龟，与海龟相对

entries.definition: a turtle that lives in the open ocean
entries.definitionCN: 生活在开阔海面的海龟

entries.definition: the hard outer covering of an animal
entries.definitionCN: 硬壳；动物的甲壳

normalIntro.en: Turtle is a shell that walks: protection first, speed last.
normalIntro.cn: turtle 是会走路的壳：先求保护，速度最后。

normal.en: A sea turtle swims with flippers and lays eggs on the sand.
normal.cn: sea turtle 用鳍状肢游泳，在沙上产卵。

normal.en: Turn turtle means to capsize.
normal.cn: turn turtle 表示翻船。

normal.en: The shell of a turtle is part of its backbone.
normal.cn: 龟的甲壳其实是它骨骼的一部分。

normal.en: Tortoise is the land cousin, turtle is the water one.
normal.cn: tortoise 是陆上的亲戚，turtle 是水中的那种。

normal.en: Compare the spelling with turtledove, which once confused scribes.
normal.cn: 对比 turtledove 的拼写，它当年曾让抄写者混淆。

abstract.en: Picture a green shell rising out of the blue water like a small island.
abstract.cn: 想象一只绿色龟壳从蓝水里升起，像一座小岛。

abstract.en: Imagine a helmet that walks very slowly on four short legs.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶头盔四条短腿慢慢走路。

abstract.en: Think of a rowboat lying flat on its belly like a flipped turtle.
abstract.cn: 想象一条划子肚皮朝上趴在风浪里，像翻了的龟。

examples.en: Every year the turtles return to the same beach to nest.
examples.cn: 每年海龟都会回到同一片海滩筑巢。

examples.en: The small fishing boat turned turtle in the storm.
examples.cn: 那条小渔船在风暴中翻了。

examples.en: A turtle moves slowly but carries its home on its back.
examples.cn: 龟行动缓慢，却把家背在背上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特偷」——海「龟」特爱偷懒在沙滩上晒壳；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 晚期拉丁语 tortuca（龟）→ 古法语 tortue → 英语受 turtledove 读音影响改拼为 turtle，核心义「带硬壳的爬行动物」。

sensesIntro.en: Turtle names first the shelled reptile, then its meat, then an upside down capsize, then cautious slowness, and finally the rolled collar.
sensesIntro.cn: turtle 先指带壳的爬行动物，再指龟肉，然后指翻个底朝天的倾覆、保守的缓慢，最后指卷起的领口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard shell that crawls slowly and hides its head.
core.cn: 核心意象：背着重壳慢慢爬行、能缩头的动物。

branches.en: The shelled reptile is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 带壳的爬行动物是基本义项。

branches.en: Its meat is a culinary extension of the name.
branches.cn: 龟肉是该词在饮食上的延伸。

branches.en: Capsizing borrows the picture of a flipped turtle.
branches.cn: 倾覆借用了龟四脚朝天的画面。

branches.en: Cautious slowness comes from the slow crawl.
branches.cn: 谨慎缓慢来自它迟缓的爬行。

branches.en: The rolled collar repeats the turtle hiding its head.
branches.cn: 翻卷的高领重复了龟缩头的画面。

intro.en: Turtle is a French borrowing with no productive Latin affix of its own, but English compounds turtleneck and turtleback around it.
intro.cn: turtle 是法语借词，本身不含能产的拉丁词缀，但英语围绕它构成了 turtleneck 与 turtleback。

latinIntro.en: The family goes back to Late Latin tortuca, not to a classical Latin verb.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族的源头是晚期拉丁语 tortuca，而不是某个古典拉丁变动词。

items.example: Tortuca is the earliest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: tortuca 是最早的书面形式。

items.example: Tortue passes into English.
items.exampleCN: tortue 传入英语。

items.example: Turtle is the modern spelling.
items.exampleCN: turtle 是现代拼写。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或活动的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms turtling.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 turtling。

items.meaning: the catching or flipping of turtles
items.meaningCN: 捕龟；掀翻龟身（旧航海用语）
items.example: Turtling was old sailors work.
items.exampleCN: turtling 是旧水手的活儿。

items.meaning: a hump shaped like a turtle shell
items.example: Turtleback names a raised deck.
items.exampleCN: turtleback 指一种隆起的甲板。

items.example: Turtleneck joins turtle and neck.
items.exampleCN: turtleneck 由 turtle 与 neck 合成。

items.example: Turn turtle keeps the flipped image.
items.exampleCN: turn turtle 保留了「翻过来」的画面。

definition_zh: 细枝；嫩枝；小枝；突然明白；领悟；察觉
definition_en: a small thin branch that grows out of a larger branch or stem, or to realize something suddenly
core_image: 一根从粗枝上分叉出来的细木条，末端还挂着几片嫩叶
scene: 春天的果园里，果农剪下一根新长的细枝嫁接。The gardener cut a young twig from the apple tree to graft it.
sceneCN: 这里 twig 是「细枝、嫩枝」（第 1 个义项）：从大枝上分出的细小木质枝条；句意：园丁从苹果树上剪下一根嫩枝用于嫁接。

derivatives.zh: 由 twig 加后缀 -y 构成，义为「细枝状的」或「瘦长的（指人）」
twig 的常规复数，义为「多根细枝」
由动词 twig 加 -ed 构成，口语中义为「被领悟的、被察觉到的」

senses.title: A small thin branch
senses.definition: a small slender branch that grows from a bigger branch or stem
senses.definitionCN: 从较大的树枝或茎干上长出的细小枝条
senses.example: The nest was hidden among the twigs at the top.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟巢藏在顶端的细枝之间。
senses.why: The oldest sense: the noun names the smallest shoot that splits off from a larger branch.
senses.whyCN: 这是最早的义项：名词指从大枝上分叉出来的最小枝条。

senses.title: A leafy cutting used for planting
senses.definition: a young twig cut from a plant and used to grow a new plant by cutting or grafting
senses.definitionCN: 从植物上剪下、用来扦插或嫁接培育新植株的嫩枝
senses.example: Softwood twigs root easily in a warm, damp soil.
senses.exampleCN: 未木质化的嫩枝在温暖潮湿的土壤里很容易生根。
senses.why: Because a young twig holds living buds, gardeners began to use the word for the twig they plant.
senses.whyCN: 嫩枝上带着活的芽，园艺里人们就把用来栽种的枝条也叫 twig。

senses.title: To realize suddenly
senses.definition: to understand or realize something suddenly, used mostly in informal British English
senses.definitionCN: 突然理解或意识到某事，多用在英式英语口语中
senses.example: It took me a second to twig what she meant.
senses.exampleCN: 我愣了一下才明白她的意思。
senses.why: The thought is pictured as a small branch that suddenly snaps into place inside the mind.
senses.whyCN: 把思绪想象成一根小枝，突然在脑海里咔地接上了，就是恍然大悟。

senses.title: To notice or spot something
senses.definition: to notice something or spot a detail, often in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 注意到某事物或看出某个细节，常用于口语
senses.example: The guard twigged the stolen bike at once.
senses.exampleCN: 警卫一眼就认出了那辆失窃的自行车。
senses.why: Realizing and noticing are nearly the same mental event, so the verb extends to spotting details.
senses.whyCN: 领悟和察觉几乎是同一个心理事件，所以动词也延伸到发现细节。

senses.title: A thin structure like a twig
senses.definition: a thin branching structure that looks like a twig in a drawing, a blood vessel, or a map
senses.definitionCN: 绘画、血管或地图中看上去像细枝的分岔结构
senses.example: On the map the lanes spread like twigs from a trunk.
senses.exampleCN: 地图上，小巷像从树干分出的细枝一样散开。
senses.why: Metaphor copies the shape of a branching twig onto any fine forked structure.
senses.whyCN: 比喻用法把分叉细枝的形状套用到任何细小的分岔结构上。

intro.en: Twig goes back to Old English twig and comes from the same Germanic root as two, meaning a fork or a split-off part.
intro.cn: twig 源自中古英语 twig，更早来自古英语 twig，与 two 同出一支日耳曼语词根，核心含义是「分叉、分出的部分」。

items.en: A reconstructed form such as twigam means a twig or a fork; the link to two is generally accepted.
items.cn: 一般认为可重构出 twigam 一类形式，义为细枝或分叉；它与 two 的联系得到普遍认可。

items.en: Twig is recorded meaning a branch or a shoot.
items.cn: 古英语 twig 记录义为树枝、嫩枝。

items.en: Twig keeps the plant sense and spreads into everyday speech.
items.cn: 中古英语 twig 保留植物含义，并进入日常用语。

items.en: Slang texts show twig as a verb meaning to understand or catch on.
items.cn: 在十八至十九世纪的俚语文本中，twig 已作为动词，义为「弄懂、明白」。

items.en: The noun stays common, and the verb survives mainly in British informal English.
items.cn: 现代英语中名词用法依然常见，动词用法则主要留在英式口语里。

note.en: Twig sits between plant words such as branch, bough, and sprig, and near verbs of realizing such as notice and catch on.
note.cn: twig 一侧是 branch、bough、sprig 这类植物词，另一侧是 notice、catch on 这类表示领悟的动词。

entries.definition: one of two children born at the same time
entries.definitionCN: 双胞胎之一；只是拼写相近，与 twig 词源不同

entries.definition: thin and branch-like, or covered with twigs
entries.definitionCN: 细枝状的；覆满细枝的（twig 加 -y 构成）

entries.definition: the soft light just before sunrise or after sunset
entries.definitionCN: 黎明或黄昏的微光；仅开头拼写相近，词源无关

entries.definition: a limb growing out from the trunk of a tree
entries.definitionCN: 树枝（比 twig 粗大）

entries.definition: a small shoot with leaves on it
entries.definitionCN: 带叶的小枝；嫩枝

entries.definition: to see or become aware of something
entries.definitionCN: 注意到；察觉（对应 twig 的动词义）

normalIntro.en: Twig is first a thin fork on a tree and later the moment a thought forks into understanding.
normalIntro.cn: twig 先是一根从树上分叉的细枝，后来成了思绪「接通」的那一刻。

normal.en: The noun comes from Old English twig, a small split-off branch.
normal.cn: 名词来自古英语 twig，义为分出来的小枝。

normal.en: Twig shares its root family with two, because a twig is a fork into two parts.
normal.cn: twig 与 two 同族，因为细枝是「一分为二」的岔。

normal.en: Twiggy is the adjective, as in a twiggy shrub or a twiggy figure.
normal.cn: 形容词是 twiggy，如「枝条繁密的灌木」或「瘦得像柴棍的身材」。

normal.en: Twig that means to realize something, as in I twigged what she meant.
normal.cn: twig that 表示明白某事，如「我明白了她的意思」。

normal.en: Compare branch, of a thick limb, with twig, of the thinnest tip.
normal.cn: 对比 branch 指粗树枝，twig 指最细的枝梢。

abstract.en: Picture a bird landing on a thin twig that bends but does not break.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鸟落在细枝上，枝条弯了却没有断。

abstract.en: Imagine a twig sticking out of a bag of garden soil, ready to become a new plant.
abstract.cn: 想象一根嫩枝插在花土袋里，正要长成新植物。

abstract.en: See a light bulb branching on like a tiny fork when you suddenly understand.
abstract.cn: 想象明白的瞬间，脑子里像细枝分叉一样啪地亮起一盏灯。

examples.en: He used a twig to draw a pattern in the sand.
examples.cn: 他用一根细枝在沙子上画图案。

examples.en: She finally twigged that the letter was a warning.
examples.cn: 她终于明白那封信是个警告。

examples.en: Birds were building nests from dry twigs.
examples.cn: 鸟儿正用干树枝筑巢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特 wig」——特别细的假发丝，其实就是一根细枝；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 twig（细枝）→ 中古英语 twig（嫩枝）→ 英语 twig；与 two（二）同出自表示「分叉」的日耳曼语词根，核心义「从大枝分出的细枝」。

sensesIntro.en: Twig starts with the physical thin branch, extends to the cutting used in planting, then moves metaphorically to a sudden mental fork of realization and noticing.
sensesIntro.cn: twig 从有形的细枝出发，延伸到扦插用的嫩枝，再借「分叉」的意象转到突然领悟、察觉，最后指细枝状的分岔结构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin twig forking out from a thick branch.
core.cn: 核心意象：细枝从粗枝上分叉出来。

branches.en: The literal thin branch is the base sense.
branches.cn: 字面的细枝是基础义项。

branches.en: A leafy young twig becomes the cutting for planting.
branches.cn: 带芽的嫩枝变成扦插用的枝条。

branches.en: The mental fork of suddenly getting it links realization and noticing.
branches.cn: 领悟与察觉共享「思绪分叉」这一心理意象。

branches.en: Any fine branching structure borrows the twig shape.
branches.cn: 任何细小的分岔结构都借用细枝的形状。

branches.en: Both a wild twig and a planted cutting are young living shoots.
branches.cn: 野生细枝与扦插枝条都是活着的幼嫩枝条。

intro.en: Twig is a short native word with no prefix; the family is grown from it by endings such as -y and by the verb ending -ed.
intro.cn: twig 是简短的英语本族词，没有前缀；词族由 -y、-ed 等词尾从它长出来。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor: twig is a Germanic word, related to two through a shared root of splitting.
latinIntro.cn: twig 没有拉丁语祖先，它是日耳曼语词，与 two 共享表示「分叉」的词根。

items.example: Twig keeps its Old English plant sense.
items.exampleCN: twig 保留了古英语的植物含义。

items.example: The ending -s forms twigs.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 twigs。

items.example: Twigs pile up under the tree.
items.exampleCN: twigs 指树下的成堆细枝。

items.example: The suffix -y forms twiggy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 twiggy。

items.example: Twiggy describes a thin branching shape.
items.exampleCN: twiggy 描述细枝般分岔的形状。

items.example: Twig as a verb is common in informal British speech.
items.exampleCN: twig 作动词常见于英式口语。

items.example: The ending -ed forms twigged.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 twigged。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms twigging.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 twigging。

items.example: Two shares the forking root of twig.
items.exampleCN: two 与 twig 共享「分叉」词根。

definition_zh: 两倍的；双重的；两方面的；两倍地；成双地
definition_en: twice as much or twice as large, or having two parts or aspects
core_image: 一张纸从中间对折，一层变成两层
scene: 商场标语说，节日促销让客流增长了两倍。The holiday campaign brought a twofold rise in foot traffic, the manager said.
sceneCN: 这里 twofold 是「两倍的」（第 1 个义项：数量翻了一番）；句意：经理说，节日活动让客流量增长了两倍。

forms.label: 无比较级（作定语形容词）

derivatives.zh: 由 twofold 加 -ness 构成，义为「双重性」
twofold 的前项词根，义为「二」，表示「二重」的来源
twofold 的后项词根，义为「倍；层；折叠」

senses.title: Twice as much or as large
senses.definition: twice as much in number, amount, or size, often after words such as increase
senses.definitionCN: 在数量、金额或规模上达到原来的两倍，常跟在 increase 等词后
senses.example: The cost of the repair was twofold that of a new unit.
senses.exampleCN: 维修的费用是新机器价格的两倍。
senses.why: The suffix -fold means times, so the word counts the layers as two.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -fold 表示「倍」，所以这个词就是把层数数成两倍。

senses.title: Having two parts or aspects
senses.definition: having two different parts, aims, or aspects at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 同时具有两个不同的部分、目的或方面
senses.example: Her decision had a twofold aim: to save money and to save time.
senses.exampleCN: 她的决定有双重目的：省钱又省时。
senses.why: A folded sheet has two layers, so twofold easily names anything with two sides.
senses.whyCN: 对折的纸有两层，因此 twofold 很自然地指任何有两面的东西。

senses.title: Two layers deep
senses.definition: folded over so that there are two thicknesses of the same material
senses.definitionCN: 折叠起来使同一种材料成为两层厚度
senses.example: The banner was fastened with a twofold band of cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 横幅是用一条对折过的布带固定的。
senses.why: The most concrete reading is the literal fold: one layer laid over another.
senses.whyCN: 最具体的解读就是字面的折叠：一层叠在另一层上。

senses.title: By two times
senses.definition: used as an adverb meaning by two times, often after a verb of change
senses.definitionCN: 作副词，表示「达到两倍」，常跟在表示变化的动词后
senses.example: Sales rose twofold in the first quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 第一季度销售额增长了两倍。
senses.why: The same folded idea shifts from describing a thing to describing the size of a change.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「折层」概念，从形容事物转而形容变化的幅度。

senses.title: For two reasons
senses.titleCN: 出于两个原因；从两方面看
senses.definition: used to point out that there are exactly two grounds or explanations for something
senses.definitionCN: 用来指出某事恰好有两个理由或两方面解释
senses.example: The plan is twofold better: it is cheaper and it is faster.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案在两方面都更好：更便宜也更快。
senses.why: Counting aspects as two follows directly from the counting sense of two.
senses.whyCN: 把方面数成两个，直接来自 two 的计数本质。

intro.en: Twofold joins two with the Old English suffix -feald, which means times or layers, the same ending seen in threefold and manifold.
intro.cn: twofold 由 two 加上古英语词尾 -feald 构成，表示「倍、层」，threefold 与 manifold 用的是同一词尾。

items.en: Twi- or two- combines with -feald to mean double.
items.cn: 古英语中 twi- 与 -feald 组合，义为「双倍」。

items.en: The form twofold is settled and used for both number and structure.
items.cn: 中古英语形式 twofold 定型，兼表数量与结构。

items.en: German zweifach and Dutch tweevoudig keep the same pattern.
items.cn: 德语 zweifach 与荷兰语 tweevoudig 保留同样的构词模式。

items.en: Twofold spreads in formal and scientific writing.
items.cn: 在十六至十七世纪，twofold 在正式与科技写作中流行起来。

items.en: The adjective is common in data and reports; the adverb is rarer.
items.cn: 现代英语中形容词常见于数据与报告，副词用法较少。

note.en: Twofold belongs to a family of number words built with -fold, and is close in meaning to double and dual.
note.cn: twofold 属于由 -fold 构成的数词家族，意思上与 double、dual 接近。

entries.definition: three times as much
entries.definitionCN: 三倍的；三重的

entries.definition: many and of several kinds
entries.definitionCN: 多样的；多方面的

entries.definition: a pair of people
entries.definitionCN: 两人一组；注意后缀不同，义为「一对」

entries.definition: twice the amount or having two parts
entries.definitionCN: 两倍的；双重的

entries.definition: having two parts that work together
entries.definitionCN: 双重的；二元的

entries.definition: two times
entries.definitionCN: 两次；两倍

normalIntro.en: Twofold is a counting word: two plus the fold that turns layers into times.
normalIntro.cn: twofold 是计数词：two 加 -fold，-fold 把「层」变成「倍」。

normal.en: -fold is the Old English ending for times or layers, as in threefold and manifold.
normal.cn: -fold 是古英语中表示「倍、层」的词尾，如 threefold、manifold。

normal.en: A twofold increase means the number doubled.
normal.cn: a twofold increase 就是数量翻了一番。

normal.en: A twofold purpose means there are two aims at once.
normal.cn: a twofold purpose 就是同时有两个目的。

normal.en: German zweifach and Dutch tweevoudig use the same pattern.
normal.cn: 德语 zweifach、荷兰语 tweevoudig 用的是同样的构词模式。

normal.en: Compare double, which is more common, with twofold, which is more formal and often used in reports.
normal.cn: 对比 double 更常用，twofold 更正式，多出现在报告里。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of paper folded once so that it has two layers.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸对折一次，变成两层。

abstract.en: See a graph line that doubles its height in one year.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上的线在一年内高了一倍。

abstract.en: Imagine a road sign with two arrows: one for money, one for time.
abstract.cn: 想象一块路牌上有两个箭头：一个指省钱，一个指省时。

examples.en: The new system produced a twofold saving in energy.
examples.cn: 新系统带来了两倍的节能效果。

examples.en: Her visit served a twofold purpose: study and rest.
examples.cn: 她的出行有双重目的：学习与休息。

examples.en: Output advanced twofold over five years.
examples.cn: 五年间产量增长了两倍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吐 fold」——吐出一口气把纸对折，就成了两层，即两倍；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 twi-（二）+ -feald（倍、层）→ 中古英语 twofold → 英语 twofold；核心义「折成两层」，引申为「翻倍、双重」。

sensesIntro.en: Twofold begins with the measurable twice-as-much sense, then moves to the two-parts sense, the literal two layers, the adverb of doubling, and finally counting two reasons.
sensesIntro.cn: twofold 先指可度量的「两倍」，再指「两个部分」，然后是字面的「双层」，接着作副词表示「成倍」，最后指「两个理由」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet folded once into two layers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张纸对折成两层。

branches.en: The quantity reading covers both the adjective and the adverb.
branches.cn: 数量义覆盖形容词与副词两种用法。

branches.en: Two aspects and two reasons are the abstract counting branch.
branches.cn: 两方面与两个原因属于抽象的计数分支。

branches.en: The literal folded layer is the base image.
branches.cn: 字面的折叠层是基础意象。

branches.en: Both a doubled amount and a double aim share the idea of two counted twice.
branches.cn: 翻倍的数量与双重的目的都共享「数到两倍」的观念。

branches.en: The adverb folds a change and its two explanations into one short word.
branches.cn: 副词用法把变化的幅度与两种解释压缩在一个短词里。

intro.en: Twofold is built from the numeral two and the suffix -fold, the productive ending that also gives threefold and many times words.
intro.cn: twofold 由数词 two 与后缀 -fold 构成，这个能产后缀还构成 threefold 等表示倍数的词。

latinIntro.en: The ending -fold is native Germanic, not Latin; there is no Latin ancestor to list.
latinIntro.cn: 词尾 -fold 是日耳曼语本族成分，并非拉丁语，因此没有可列的拉丁同源词。

items.example: Two supplies the first half of twofold.
items.exampleCN: two 是 twofold 的前半部分。

items.example: The suffix -fold turns a number into times.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -fold 把数字变成「几倍」。

items.example: Twofold is mostly used before a noun or after increase.
items.exampleCN: twofold 多用于名词前或 increase 之后。

items.example: Threefold replaces two with three.
items.exampleCN: threefold 只是把 two 换成了 three。

items.example: Fourfold follows the same pattern.
items.exampleCN: fourfold 遵循同样的模式。

items.example: Manifold shows how wide -fold can go.
items.exampleCN: manifold 显示 -fold 的用法可以很宽。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ness forms twofoldness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 twofoldness。

items.example: Twofoldness names the double state.
items.exampleCN: twofoldness 指双重的性质。

items.example: Double is the everyday twin of twofold.
items.exampleCN: double 是 twofold 的日常对等词。

definition_zh: 打字错误；排印错误；笔误；排印错误（作为集合）；打字错误（复数）
definition_en: a small mistake made when typing or printing a word
core_image: 键盘上一根手指按错了键，屏幕上多出一个歪掉的字母
scene: 论文打印出来拿给导师看，导师用红笔圈出一个拼错的单词。The professor circled a typo in the introduction of my essay.
sceneCN: 这里 typo 是「打字错误」（第 1 个义项：打字时敲错字）；句意：教授圈出了我论文引言里的一个打字错误。

collocations.zh: 拼写疏漏（口语冗余说法）

derivatives.zh: 由 typography 加 -al 构成，义为「排印的、印刷的」，是 typo 的长派生形式
与 typo 同源的 -graphy 名词，义为「排印术、字体排印」
与 typo 同源的 -ist 名词，义为「打字员」

senses.title: A mistake made while typing
senses.definition: a small error in a typed text, usually a wrong or missing letter
senses.definitionCN: 在打出的文本中出现的细小错误，通常是字母打错或漏打
senses.example: There is a typo in the second line of the email.
senses.exampleCN: 邮件的第二行有一个打字错误。
senses.why: Typo is clipped from typographical error, so it names any slip made on a keyboard.
senses.whyCN: typo 是 typographical error 的缩略，所以泛指在键盘上敲错的地方。

senses.title: A printing or typesetting slip
senses.definition: an error that appears in printed text because of a typesetting mistake
senses.definitionCN: 因排版失误而出现在印刷文本里的错误
senses.example: The first edition contains a typo on every tenth page.
senses.exampleCN: 第一版每十页就有一处排印错误。
senses.why: Before computers, the word lived in print shops, where type was set by hand.
senses.whyCN: 在电脑出现之前，这个词活跃在活字排印的印坊里。

senses.title: A small error in spelling or writing
senses.definition: a small and usually harmless error in spelling or writing that readers can easily correct
senses.definitionCN: 拼写或书写上细小、通常无伤大雅、读者一看就能改正的错误
senses.example: She noticed a typo in the heading of the report.
senses.exampleCN: 她发现报告标题里有个笔误。
senses.why: Once typing spread, the word widened to cover any small slip of the hand or thumb.
senses.whyCN: 打字普及之后，这个词扩展到手指或拇指滑一下造成的任何小错。

senses.title: The wrong key pressed
senses.titleCN: 打错的字符（多出一个字母等）
senses.definition: the specific wrong letter or character that appears because the wrong key was pressed
senses.definitionCN: 因按错键而出现的那个错误字母或字符
senses.example: A single typo turned their address into an unsafe link.
senses.exampleCN: 仅仅一个打错的字母就把他们的网址变成了不安全的链接。
senses.why: This is the most concrete reading: the visible character that should not be there.
senses.whyCN: 这是最具体的解读：本该不出现的那个可见字符。

senses.title: Typos as a group
senses.definition: typing errors viewed as a whole category, as in a list of typos to fix
senses.definitionCN: 把打字错误看成一整类，如待修改的错字清单
senses.example: The editor sent back a list of typos in the final draft.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑把终稿里的一串错字清单退了回来。
senses.why: The plural typos often works as a collective name for the whole class of slips.
senses.whyCN: 复数 typos 常作为整个错字类别总称来用。

intro.en: Typo is a clipped form of typographical error, and its root goes through Greek typos, meaning a blow or an impression, to type and print.
intro.cn: typo 是 typographical error 的缩略形式，词根经希腊语 typos（一击、印痕）一路走到 type 与 print。

items.en: Typos means a blow or a mark stamped into something.
items.cn: 希腊语 typos 意为击打或戳印出的印记。

items.en: Typus keeps the sense of a figure or an image.
items.cn: 拉丁语 typus 保留图形、印记的含义。

items.en: Type comes to mean a printed character used in a printing press.
items.cn: 十八世纪英语中 type 开始指印刷机用的活字。

items.en: Typographical error is shortened into the informal typo.
items.cn: 十九世纪，typographical error 被口语缩略成 typo。

items.en: Typo now means any typing mistake, on paper, on a screen, or in a message.
items.cn: 现代英语的 typo 已指任何打字错误，无论是纸上、屏幕上还是消息里。

note.en: Typo is a short, informal clipping that sits near spelling-family words and near mistakes such as slip and misprint.
note.cn: typo 是短小的口语缩略词，一侧挨着 spelling 家族，另一侧挨着 slip、misprint 这类小错。

entries.definition: to press keys to put words into a computer
entries.definitionCN: 打字；敲键盘输入文字

entries.definition: a person whose job is typing
entries.definitionCN: 打字员

entries.definition: the art of setting and arranging printed text
entries.definitionCN: 排印术；字体排印

entries.definition: a small careless mistake
entries.definitionCN: 小失误

entries.definition: a mistake in a printed text
entries.definitionCN: 印刷错误

entries.definition: something done wrongly
entries.definitionCN: 错误（泛指）

normalIntro.en: Typo is a cut-down word: it keeps the first four letters of typographical and drops the rest.
normalIntro.cn: typo 是缩略词：只留 typographical 的前四个字母，其余都省掉了。

normal.en: Typo comes from typographical error, so it is short for a printing or typing error.
normal.cn: typo 来自 typographical error，是「排印或打字错误」的简称。

normal.en: The base word type means to press keys, so a typo happens at the keyboard.
normal.cn: 基础词 type 表示敲键盘，所以 typo 发生在键盘上。

normal.en: The plural is typos, without an extra e before the s.
normal.cn: 复数是 typos，在 s 之前不加 e。

normal.en: Compare typist and typography, which keep the longer Greek root typos.
normal.cn: 对比 typist 与 typography，它们保留了更长的希腊词根 typos。

normal.en: In app design a typo is a cheap-looking mistake, so proofreading still matters.
normal.cn: 在应用设计里，typo 显得很廉价，所以校对依然重要。

abstract.en: Picture a finger hitting the key next to the right one.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指按到了正确键旁边的那一格。

abstract.en: See a metal type block sitting in a printing press with one letter upside down.
abstract.cn: 想象印刷机里一块活字，有一个字母放倒了。

abstract.en: Imagine reading a menu that says soup of the dau instead of soup of the day.
abstract.cn: 想象菜单上把「今日例汤」的一个字母打错，读起来很滑稽。

examples.en: Please check the document for typos before printing.
examples.cn: 打印前请检查文档里有没有打字错误。

examples.en: He made a typo when he typed the password.
examples.cn: 他输入密码时打错了一个字。

examples.en: A typo on the poster changed the date of the concert.
examples.cn: 海报上一个打字错误把音乐会日期弄错了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太破」——键盘太破了，老按错键，出一堆打字错误；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 typos（击打、印痕）→ 拉丁语 typus（印记、图形）→ 英语 type（活字、打字）→ typographical error → 缩略为 typo，核心义「敲出的一处小错」。

sensesIntro.en: Typo starts as a keyboard slip, broadens to a printing or typesetting error, then to any small spelling slip, then to the wrong character itself, and finally to the whole class of such errors.
sensesIntro.cn: typo 从敲键盘的小错出发，扩展到排印错误，再泛指笔误，然后特指那个多出来的错误字符，最后作为整类错字的总称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pressing the wrong key.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指按错了键。

branches.en: The keyboard slip and the spelling slip are the everyday core.
branches.cn: 键盘打字错与拼写笔误是日常核心义。

branches.en: The print-shop sense preserves the history of movable type.
branches.cn: 排印义保留了活字印刷的历史。

branches.en: The wrong character is the concrete trace of the mistake.
branches.cn: 错误字符是失误留下的具体痕迹。

branches.en: The plural typos gathers all the slips into one class.
branches.cn: 复数 typos 把所有错字归为一类。

branches.en: A single typo and a list of typos differ only in scale.
branches.cn: 单个错字与错字清单只在规模上有别。

intro.en: Typo is really a double clipping: the full phrase typographical error keeps only the first four letters and becomes a noun of its own.
intro.cn: typo 其实是一个双重缩略：完整短语 typographical error 只留下前四个字母，独立成词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin form typus means an image or a stamp, from which the modern meaning of type as a printed character grew.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形式 typus 意为图像、印痕，现代英语 type 作「活字」的含义就从这里长出。

items.example: The root typo- appears in typography.
items.exampleCN: 词根 typo- 出现在 typography 中。

items.example: Type was set by hand in early presses.
items.exampleCN: 早期印刷机的活字是手工排的。

items.example: You type a message much faster on a keyboard.
items.exampleCN: 用键盘打消息要快得多。

items.example: Typographical error is the full phrase behind typo.
items.exampleCN: typographical error 是 typo 的完整表达。

items.meaningCN: 表示「书写、记录、工艺」的词尾
items.example: The suffix -graphy forms typography.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -graphy 构成 typography。

items.example: Typography is where typos come from.
items.exampleCN: 排印术正是 typo 的来源。

items.example: A careful typist makes few typos.
items.exampleCN: 细心的打字员很少打错字。

items.example: Typo is the clipped everyday name.
items.exampleCN: typo 是日常使用的缩略名。

items.example: The ending -s forms typos.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 typos。

definition_zh: 霸王龙；暴龙（白垩纪晚期的大型肉食恐龙）；暴君般的庞然大物；喻指专横霸道的强人
definition_en: a huge meat-eating dinosaur of the late Cretaceous, with a massive head and tiny front limbs; also a by-name for a bullying giant or an overbearing person
core_image: 一具比树干还长的巨大头骨配一对短短的小前肢，停在化石坑里
scene: 博物馆展厅中央，骨架比天花板还高，孩子们仰头数它嘴里的大牙。In the centre of the museum hall a skeleton rises higher than the ceiling, and children tilt their heads to count the huge teeth in the mouth of a tyrannosaurus.
sceneCN: 这里 tyrannosaurus 指「霸王龙这种恐龙」（第 1 个义项：化石与博物馆语境里的恐龙本身）；句意：展厅中央一具骨架比天花板还高，孩子们仰头数霸王龙嘴里的大牙。场景要点：高过天花板的骨架、一排大牙、仰头张望的孩子。

pos.zh: 庞然大物；暴君般的强者

collocations.zh: 暴龙（学名，意为「君王暴君蜥蜴」）
一头企业霸王龙（喻指垄断巨头）

derivatives.zh: 去掉拉丁词尾 -us 的常见简化形式，泛指暴龙类成员
属名 + 种名，种名 rex 意为「君王」，即「君王暴君蜥蜴」
古生物学术语：暴龙科成员或暴龙科的

senses.title: A tyrannosaur dinosaur
senses.definition: a very large two-legged meat-eating dinosaur, famous for its huge jaws and tiny arms
senses.definitionCN: 一种用两条后腿行走的大型肉食恐龙，以巨大的下颚和极小的前肢著称
senses.example: The museum mounted a complete tyrannosaurus on the main floor.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆在主展厅组装了一具完整的霸王龙骨架。
senses.why: The Greek name literally says tyrant lizard, and the genus was given this name for its size and fearsome jaws.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语名字字面就是「暴君蜥蜴」，命名者正是被它的体型和可怕的下颚震撼，才给它起了这个名。

senses.title: The fossil genus Tyrannosaurus
senses.titleCN: 暴龙属；霸王龙化石与标本
senses.definition: the scientific genus name, usually written with a capital letter, for fossils and specimens of these animals
senses.definitionCN: 作为科学属名的用法，首字母大写，用于指这类动物的化石与标本
senses.example: Tyrannosaurus rex lived in what is now western North America.
senses.exampleCN: 暴龙生活在今天的北美西部一带。
senses.why: Scientific naming gives the animal a genus label, so the word becomes a proper noun in palaeontology.
senses.whyCN: 科学命名给动物一个属的标签，于是这个词在古生物学里变成了专有名词，写法也带上大写和大写的属名。

senses.title: A giant that devours everything
senses.definition: figuratively, a huge powerful force that crushes or swallows whatever lies around it
senses.definitionCN: 比喻义：一股巨大而强大的力量，碾碎或吞掉周围的一切
senses.example: The new supermarket chain is a retail tyrannosaurus.
senses.exampleCN: 这家新连锁超市是一头零售业的霸王龙。
senses.why: A predator at the top of its food chain becomes a natural metaphor for anything huge that eats smaller rivals.
senses.whyCN: 站在食物链顶端的掠食者，天然成为「吞掉小竞争对手的庞然大物」的比喻。

senses.title: An overbearing person
senses.definition: a dominating, bullying person, especially one who treats others like prey
senses.definitionCN: 专横、欺压他人的人，尤指把别人当猎物对待的家伙
senses.example: Our manager is a kindly little tyrannosaurus in a suit.
senses.exampleCN: 我们经理是个穿西装的小个子霸王龙，专横得很。
senses.why: The tyrant half of the name links the dinosaur to tyrants, so it can label a domestic bully.
senses.whyCN: 名字里的「暴君」一半把恐龙和暴君连在一起，所以它也能用来称呼身边专横的人。

intro.en: Tyrannosaurus is a scientific name coined in 1905 from Greek tyrannos, tyrant, and sauros, lizard, with the Latin ending -us.
intro.cn: tyrannosaurus 是 1905 年造出的科学名称，由希腊语 tyrannos（暴君）与 sauros（蜥蜴）加上拉丁词尾 -us 组成。

items.en: Greek tyrannos means an absolute ruler who holds power without legal right.
items.cn: 希腊语 tyrannos 意为不凭合法权利掌权的专制君主。

items.en: Greek sauros means lizard, and it names many dinosaurs.
items.cn: 希腊语 sauros 意为蜥蜴，是许多恐龙名称的构词成分。

items.en: Latin tyranus is borrowed from Greek and passes the word on to English tyrant and tyranny.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tyranus 借自希腊语，把这个词传给英语的 tyrant 与 tyranny。

items.en: Palaeontologist Henry Fairfield Osborn creates the genus name Tyrannosaurus, meaning tyrant lizard.
items.cn: 古生物学家奥斯本在一九零五年造出属名 Tyrannosaurus，意为「暴君蜥蜴」。

items.en: English takes the name as a common noun, and the short form T rex spreads in popular culture.
items.cn: 英语把它借作普通名词，缩略形式 T rex 又在流行文化中传开。

items.en: The word gains the figurative senses of an overwhelming giant or a bullying person.
items.cn: 这个词又衍生出「势不可挡的庞然大物」与「专横之人」的比喻义。

note.en: Tyrannosaurus belongs to the lizard-named dinosaur family and sits near words for tyrants and predators.
note.cn: tyrannosaurus 属于「蜥蜴」命名的恐龙词族，同时与「暴君」「掠食者」这些词相邻。

entries.definition: a reptile of the Mesozoic era
entries.definitionCN: 中生代的爬行动物；恐龙

entries.definition: a huge long-necked plant-eating dinosaur
entries.definitionCN: 一种长颈的大型植食恐龙

entries.definition: a cruel ruler who uses power unjustly
entries.definitionCN: 残暴不公地使用权力的统治者；暴君

entries.definition: an animal that hunts and eats others
entries.definitionCN: 捕食其他动物的掠食者

entries.definition: a meat-eating dinosaur that walked on two legs
entries.definitionCN: 两足行走的肉食恐龙；兽脚类

entries.definition: an enormous and powerful thing or organization
entries.definitionCN: 巨大的庞然大物或巨型机构

normalIntro.en: Tyrannosaurus is tyrant plus lizard, so the name already contains a tiny joke about a bullying reptile.
normalIntro.cn: tyrannosaurus 等于暴君加蜥蜴，名字本身就藏着一个「专横爬行动物」的小玩笑。

normal.en: Break it as tyran- plus -saurus: tyrant lizard.
normal.cn: 拆成 tyran- 加 -saurus：暴君蜥蜴。

normal.en: The end -saurus appears in brontosaurus and pterosaur, all dinosaur names.
normal.cn: 词尾 -saurus 也出现在 brontosaurus 与 pterosaur 等恐龙名称里。

normal.en: The species name rex means king, so the full name says king tyrant lizard.
normal.cn: 种名 rex 意为国王，所以全名说的是「君王暴君蜥蜴」。

normal.en: Tiny arms and huge jaws are the classic picture: power concentrated in the head.
normal.cn: 小前肢加大下颚是经典画面：力量集中在头部。

normal.en: Compare tyrant and tyranny, which carry the same cruel-rule core.
normal.cn: 对比 tyrant 与 tyranny，它们共享同样的「残暴统治」内核。

abstract.en: Picture a lizard wearing a crown and stomping over smaller animals.
abstract.cn: 想象一只戴着王冠的蜥蜴，踩过一群小动物。

abstract.en: Think of a filing label on a museum drawer with a capital T and a Latin-looking ending.
abstract.cn: 想象博物馆抽屉上的标签，一个首字母大写，词尾带着拉丁味。

abstract.en: Imagine a shark-like appetite inside a body the size of a bus.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆公交车大小的身体里装着鲨鱼般的胃口。

examples.en: Tyrannosaurus rex probably had a bite far stronger than any living land animal.
examples.cn: 霸王龙的咬合力很可能远超任何现存的陆生动物。

examples.en: Children love the tyrannosaurus more than any other skeleton in the hall.
examples.cn: 孩子们最喜欢大厅里那具霸王龙骨架，胜过其他任何一具。

examples.en: The oil company has grown into a tyrannosaurus that swallows small rivals.
examples.cn: 这家石油公司已经长成一头吞掉小竞争对手的霸王龙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踢烂楼 · 坐死」——想象它一踢就踢烂一栋楼，一坐就把猎物坐死；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关（词源是希腊语「暴君蜥蜴」）。

root: 希腊语 tyrannos（暴君）+ sauros（蜥蜴）+ 拉丁词尾 -us → 现代拉丁属名 Tyrannosaurus（暴君蜥蜴），英语借用为普通名词。

sensesIntro.en: Tyrannosaurus starts as the animal, becomes the scientific genus label, and then extends to any huge devouring force and to a bullying person.
sensesIntro.cn: tyrannosaurus 先指这种动物本身，再成为科学属名，之后扩展为任何吞掉一切的庞然大物和专横霸道的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a giant lizard with tiny arms and a crown-like name.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只小前肢、戴着王冠般名字的巨型蜥蜴。

branches.en: The animal itself is the everyday museum sense.
branches.cn: 动物本身是博物馆语境里的日常义项。

branches.en: The genus name turns the word into a scientific label.
branches.cn: 属名把这个词变成科学标签。

branches.en: A devouring giant is the figurative business sense.
branches.cn: 吞掉一切的庞然大物是商业比喻义。

branches.en: An overbearing person borrows the tyrant half of the name.
branches.cn: 专横之人借用了名字里「暴君」的那一半。

branches.en: All three share the picture of something huge that crushes whatever it meets.
branches.cn: 三个义项共享同一个画面：巨大的东西碾压所遇到的一切。

intro.en: Tyrannosaurus builds on the Greek pieces tyranno- and -saurus, both still productive in scientific naming.
intro.cn: tyrannosaurus 由希腊语成分 tyranno- 与 -saurus 构成，这两个成分在科学命名里仍然能产。

latinIntro.en: The name is modern Latin, but it rests on Greek tyrannos and sauros and takes the Latin adjective ending -us.
latinIntro.cn: 这个名字是现代拉丁语，但底层是希腊语 tyrannos 与 sauros，并采用拉丁形容词词尾 -us。

items.example: Tyranno- is the tyrant half of the name.
items.exampleCN: tyranno- 是名字里表示暴君的那一半。

items.example: Tyrannos gave English tyrant and tyranny.
items.exampleCN: tyrannos 给出了英语的 tyrant 与 tyranny。

items.example: The suffix -saurus names many dinosaurs.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -saurus 命名了许多恐龙。

items.example: Sauros is the lizard element.
items.exampleCN: sauros 就是「蜥蜴」这一成分。

items.example: The genus was named in 1905.
items.exampleCN: 这个属名造于一九零五年。

items.example: The ending -us marks the genus as masculine.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -us 把这个属标为阳性。

items.meaning: any member of the tyrannosaur group
items.example: Tyrannosaur drops the Latin ending.
items.exampleCN: tyrannosaur 去掉了拉丁词尾。

items.example: The suffix -id gives tyrannosaurid.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -id 构成 tyrannosaurid。

items.meaning: a member of the tyrannosaur family
items.example: Tyrannosaurid is used in palaeontology.
items.exampleCN: tyrannosaurid 用于古生物学。

definition_zh: （动机）隐藏的；不可告人的；更远的；在更远处的；更晚的；进一步的
definition_en: hidden or kept from view, usually of a motive; also lying beyond what is stated or seen, farther away, or coming later
core_image: 一扇半掩的门，真正的心思藏在门后的那间房里
scene: 同事主动请缨替她做报表，她嘴上道谢，心里却在琢磨这人有没有别的心思。A colleague offered to finish her report; she thanked him, but suspected an ulterior motive behind the courtesy.
sceneCN: 这里 ulterior 是「隐藏的、不可告人的」（第 1 个义项：藏在表面理由之后的动机）；句意：同事主动提出帮她做完报表，她道了谢，却怀疑这份殷勤背后另有企图。场景要点：一句客气的主动提议、一句被咽下去的追问、藏在明面理由背后的小算盘。

pos.zh: 更远的；在更远处的；在表面之外的
更晚的；后来的；进一步的

collocations.zh: 隐藏的动机；不可告人的目的

collocations.phrase: in the ulterior parts of the building

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「暗地里；在更远处」，现代英语中很罕见
与 ulterior 同出于拉丁语 ulter（在彼方），指极端的、激进的，或极端主义者
同一词源家族的最高级形式，源于拉丁语 ultimus（最远的），义为「最终的；根本的」

senses.title: Hidden behind a stated reason
senses.definition: kept out of sight, especially of a motive that lies behind the reason given openly
senses.definitionCN: 被隐藏起来的，尤指藏在公开理由之后、不愿被人看见的动机
senses.example: He denied having any ulterior motive for the gift.
senses.exampleCN: 他否认送这份礼另有意图。
senses.why: Latin ulter means beyond, so the real push sits beyond the reason that is offered first.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ulter 意为「在彼方」，真正的推动力就待在最先说出口的理由之外。

senses.title: Beyond the visible line
senses.titleCN: 在更远处的；在有界的那一侧
senses.definition: lying beyond a boundary or line, on the farther side of something
senses.definitionCN: 位于某条界线之外、在某个东西更远的那一侧
senses.example: The ulterior rooms of the gallery are closed to visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 画廊更靠里的房间不对参观者开放。
senses.why: Latin ulter already means on the far side, so the adjective simply points to what lies past a boundary.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ulter 本就表示「在那一边」，所以这个形容词直接指向越过界线之后的东西。

senses.title: Farther out in space
senses.definition: situated farther away, at a greater distance from the point of reference
senses.definitionCN: 位置离参照点更远、距离更大的
senses.example: The ulterior provinces lay beyond the forest.
senses.exampleCN: 更偏远的外省位于森林那一边。
senses.why: The core image is simply farther away, so the word can describe distance itself.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象本来就是「更远的那一边」，所以它可以直接描述空间距离。

senses.title: Farther on in time
senses.definition: coming at a later moment, or belonging to a later stage
senses.definitionCN: 出现在更晚的时刻，或属于更后面的阶段
senses.example: He asked us to deal with ulterior matters after the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他让我们散会后再处理后续的事。
senses.why: If beyond is a place, it can also be a later point on the line of time.
senses.whyCN: 如果「彼方」是空间，它也就可以是时间线上更靠后的那一点。

senses.title: A further step or purpose
senses.titleCN: 进一步的；在表面之外的
senses.definition: additional and not yet stated, used of aims, purposes, or consequences
senses.definitionCN: 额外的、尚未明说的，用于目的、打算或后果
senses.example: The clause has an ulterior effect on small firms.
senses.exampleCN: 这一条款对小型企业还有更深一层的影响。
senses.why: Beyond the plain meaning there may be a second purpose, so the word can name that extra layer.
senses.whyCN: 在字面意义之外还可能藏着第二层目的，这个词于是可以指那多出来的一层。

intro.en: Ulterior is a Latin comparative of ulter, beyond, borrowed into English in the seventeen hundreds; the motive sense is a later narrowing.
intro.cn: ulterior 是拉丁语 ulter（在彼方）的比较级，十七世纪被借入英语；「隐藏动机」这一用法是后来收窄的结果。

items.en: Latin ulter and the adverb ultra mean beyond or on the far side.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ulter 与副词 ultra 意为「在彼方、越过那一边」。

items.en: The comparative ulterior means farther, or more remote.
items.cn: 其比较级 ulterior 意为「更远的、更偏远的」。

items.en: The superlative ultimus means farthest or last, and gives ultimate.
items.cn: 其最高级 ultimus 意为「最远的、最后的」，后来生出 ultimate。

items.en: English borrows ulterior as a learned adjective meaning farther or beyond.
items.cn: 英语以书面语身份借入 ulterior，意为「更远的、在彼方的」。

items.en: An ulterior motive is a purpose lying beyond the one declared openly.
items.cn: 「隐藏的动机」就是一桩藏在公开目的之外的打算。

items.en: Today the hidden-motive sense dominates, and the literal senses are literary or archaic.
items.cn: 今天「隐藏动机」义占绝对主导，字面义项只在书面或古雅语境中残留。

note.en: Ulterior belongs to the Latin beyond family and sits beside words for hidden purposes.
note.cn: ulterior 属于拉丁语「在彼方」词族，并与表示「隐藏目的」的词相邻。

entries.definition: final, or most basic
entries.definitionCN: 最终的；根本的（与 ulterior 同出拉丁语 ulter）

entries.definition: extreme, or an extremist
entries.definitionCN: 极端的；极端主义者（同出拉丁语 ultra）

entries.definition: second to last
entries.definitionCN: 倒数第二的（paene 几乎 + ultimus 最远）

entries.definition: not visible or not made known
entries.definitionCN: 隐藏的；未公开的

entries.definition: secret and deliberately not admitted
entries.definitionCN: 秘密的；暗中进行的

entries.definition: present but not obvious, as a cause
entries.definitionCN: 潜藏的；根本性的

normalIntro.en: Ulterior is the beyond word: whatever it describes lies past the first thing you see or hear.
normalIntro.cn: ulterior 是「在彼方」之词：它修饰的东西，总在第一眼看到或第一句听到的事之后。

normal.en: The only everyday collocation is ulterior motive, meaning a hidden reason for acting.
normal.cn: 最常用的搭配就是「隐藏动机」，即行动背后不示人的理由。

normal.en: Break it as ulter plus -ior: beyond, then the comparative ending more.
normal.cn: 拆成 ulter 加 -ior：先是「在彼方」，再加表示「更」的比较级词尾。

normal.en: The same family gives ultimate, ultra, and penultimate, all about far or last.
normal.cn: 同族给出 ultimate、ultra 与 penultimate，都围绕「远」或「最后」。

normal.en: In legal and literary prose ulterior still means farther or later on the line.
normal.cn: 在法律与文学文本里，ulterior 仍指「更远」或「时间上更晚」。

normal.en: Compare covert and underlying: covert hides on purpose, underlying lies deeper, ulterior lies past the stated reason.
normal.cn: 对比 covert 与 underlying：covert 是有意隐藏，underlying 是沉得更深，ulterior 则是躲在已经说出的理由之后。

abstract.en: Picture a gift box with a second, smaller box hidden inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一个礼盒里还藏着一个更小的盒子。

abstract.en: Draw a line and put the real intention on the far side of it.
abstract.cn: 画一条线，把真正的心思放到线的另一侧。

abstract.en: Imagine a salesman smiling while his hand is behind his back.
abstract.cn: 想象一个满脸笑容、手却藏在背后的推销员。

examples.en: She agreed to the plan, though she sensed an ulterior purpose behind it.
examples.cn: 她同意了这项计划，尽管她察觉到背后另有目的。

examples.en: The ulterior motive behind the donation became clear months later.
examples.cn: 这笔捐款背后的隐藏动机几个月后才显露出来。

examples.en: Old maps show an ulterior range of hills beyond the river.
examples.cn: 旧地图显示河流之外还有一道更远的山岭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「偶替惹」——有人突然替你做这做那，多半是惹上了什么别的心思；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ulter（在彼方）→ 比较级 ulterior（更远的）→ 英语 ulterior，核心义「在明面之外、在更远的那一边」；同族有 ultra、ultimate。

sensesIntro.en: Ulterior runs from the farthest side in space, to a later stage in time, to a purpose kept beyond the stated reason.
sensesIntro.cn: ulterior 从空间上「更远的另一侧」，走到时间上「更晚的阶段」，最后落到藏在公开理由之外的目的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door slightly open, with the real thought kept in the room behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇半掩的门，真正的心思留在门后的房间里。

branches.en: A hidden motive is the dominant modern sense.
branches.cn: 隐藏的动机是今天最主要的义项。

branches.en: Both the motive and the extra purpose live past the stated reason.
branches.cn: 隐藏动机与额外目的都待在已经说出的理由之后。

branches.en: Space senses place things beyond a line or farther away.
branches.cn: 空间义项把事物放在界线之外或更远处。

branches.en: Time uses the same beyond image for a later stage.
branches.cn: 时间义项用同一幅「彼方」画面表示更晚的阶段。

branches.en: All three share the idea of something on the far side of the obvious.
branches.cn: 三者共享同一个想法：某个东西位于显而易见之物的另一侧。

intro.en: Ulterior is built on Latin ulter with the comparative ending -ior; the family also yields the prefix ultra- and the adjective ultimate.
intro.cn: ulterior 由拉丁语 ulter 加比较级词尾 -ior 构成；同一词族还给出前缀 ultra- 与形容词 ultimate。

latinIntro.en: Latin ulter is a relic comparative meaning beyond, with ultra as its adverb and ultimus as its superlative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ulter 是一个残留的比较级，意为「在彼方」，副词作 ultra，最高级作 ultimus。

items.example: Ulter is the relic base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: ulter 是整个词族的残留基式。

items.example: The ending -ior turns ulter into ulterior.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ior 把 ulter 变成 ulterior。

items.example: Ulterior entered English in the 17c.
items.exampleCN: ulterior 在十七世纪进入英语。

items.example: Ultra is the adverb of ulter.
items.exampleCN: ultra 是 ulter 的副词形式。

items.example: The prefix ultra- forms ultrathin and ultrafast.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ultra- 构成 ultrathin 与 ultrafast。

items.example: Ultimus is the superlative of ulter.
items.exampleCN: ultimus 是 ulter 的最高级。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms ultimate.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 构成 ultimate。

items.example: Ultimate comes from ultimus.
items.exampleCN: ultimate 出自 ultimus。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms ulteriorly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 ulteriorly。

items.example: Ulteriorly is rare in modern prose.
items.exampleCN: ulteriorly 在现代书面语中很罕见。

definition_zh: 超洁净的；极度清洁的；无尘的；几乎不含杂质的；（从环境到工艺）极其卫生的
definition_en: extremely clean, free of dust, germs, or impurities, used of rooms, surfaces, fuels, and industrial processes
core_image: 芯片车间里，一个穿连体无尘服的人推着一片晶圆，空气里连一粒尘都没有
scene: 芯片车间的门口，每个进去的人都要换上连体服，用风淋吹掉身上每一粒灰尘。At the entrance to the chip plant, everyone puts on a full-body suit and is blown clean in an air shower before entering the ultraclean room.
sceneCN: 这里 ultraclean 是「超洁净的、无尘的」（第 1 个义项：洁净到没有可察觉灰尘的等级）；句意：芯片厂入口，每个人都要换上连体服，先经风淋吹净身上的灰尘，才能进入超净间。场景要点：连体服、风淋门、几乎看不见尘埃的空气。

pos.zh: 超洁净的；极度清洁的；无尘的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词词尾 -ness 构成，义为「超洁净程度」，多出现在技术说明中
带连字符的常见异拼，发音与意思完全相同，出现在部分商标与产品名中
超洁净的典型场景名词：以控制尘埃为标准的房间，常与 ultraclean 连用

senses.title: Clean beyond ordinary standards
senses.definition: cleaned to a level far beyond normal hygiene, with almost no dust, particles, or germs
senses.definitionCN: 清洁程度远超日常卫生标准，几乎没有灰尘、微粒或细菌
senses.example: Sensors are assembled in an ultraclean room.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器在超净间里组装。
senses.why: The prefix ultra- pushes the base word clean past every ordinary degree.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 ultra- 把基本词 clean 推到超出一切日常程度的位置。

senses.title: Extremely pure or refined
senses.titleCN: 几乎不含杂质的；超纯的
senses.definition: of fuels, metals, or chemicals, containing extremely little sulfur, waste, or other impurities
senses.definitionCN: 用于燃料、金属或化学品：几乎不含硫、废料或其他杂质
senses.example: The city is switching buses to ultraclean diesel.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市正把公交车改用超清洁柴油。
senses.why: Anything not wanted inside a material is dirt, so clean extends from surfaces to the content of fuels.
senses.whyCN: 材料里任何不该有的东西都算「脏」，于是 clean 从表面延伸到燃料的内部成分。

senses.title: Using near-zero-waste processes
senses.titleCN: 采用近乎零排放工艺的
senses.definition: describing manufacturing or energy technology that produces almost no pollutant or waste
senses.definitionCN: 描述几乎不产生污染物或废料的制造与能源技术
senses.example: The plant advertises an ultraclean production line.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂标榜一条超洁净生产线。
senses.why: In phrases like ultraclean coal, clean has moved from surfaces and substances to whole processes.
senses.whyCN: 在「超清洁煤」一类说法里，clean 已经从表面和物质层面移到整个工艺流程上。

senses.title: Spotless in appearance
senses.titleCN: 一尘不染的；外表洁净如新的
senses.definition: looking perfectly clean on the surface, as of a showroom, lab, or new appliance
senses.definitionCN: 表面看上去完全洁净，如展厅、实验室或新电器那样
senses.example: The showroom looked ultraclean under the white lights.
senses.exampleCN: 展厅在白色灯光下显得一尘不染。
senses.why: The core image is visual: no speck of dust can be seen at all.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是视觉的：根本看不见一粒灰尘。

intro.en: Ultraclean is a modern compound: Latin ultra, beyond, plus the plain English word clean.
intro.cn: ultraclean 是现代复合词：拉丁语 ultra（越过、超出）加上普通的英语词 clean。

items.en: Latin ultra means beyond, and it is related to ulter, the far side.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ultra 意为「越过」，与表示「彼方」的 ulter 同源。

items.en: English clean goes back to a Germanic word meaning bright and clear.
items.cn: 英语 clean 可上溯到一个日耳曼语词，意为「明亮的、清楚的」。

items.en: The prefix ultra- spreads in English, first as beyond, then as extreme.
items.cn: 前缀 ultra- 在十九世纪英语中扩散开来，先表「越过」，后表「极端」。

items.en: Clean rooms, water, and fuels are given the ultra- label for their near-zero contamination.
items.cn: 超级净间、超纯水与超清洁燃料都以 ultra- 标记其近乎为零的污染。

items.en: Ultraclean now covers chips, hospitals, vehicles, and even advertising claims.
items.cn: ultraclean 现在覆盖芯片、医院、车辆，甚至广告宣传语。

note.en: Ultraclean joins the ultra- family of intensifiers and sits with words for purity and sterility.
note.cn: ultraclean 属于 ultra- 这一强调整词族，并与「纯净」「无菌」一类词相邻。

entries.definition: a prefix meaning beyond or extremely
entries.definitionCN: 意为「超越、极度」的前缀

entries.definition: using sound above human hearing
entries.definitionCN: 使用高于人耳听觉范围的超声波的

entries.definition: light beyond the violet end of the spectrum
entries.definitionCN: 位于光谱紫端之外的光；紫外线

entries.definition: free of living bacteria and germs
entries.definitionCN: 无菌的；无微生物的

entries.definition: perfectly clean in appearance
entries.definitionCN: 一尘不染的；完美洁净的

entries.definition: extremely clean and tidy
entries.definitionCN: 极其洁净、整洁的

normalIntro.en: Ultraclean is simply ultra plus clean, so it names a level of cleanliness pushed past every normal limit.
normalIntro.cn: ultraclean 就是 ultra 加 clean，标出被推到一切普通限度之外的清洁等级。

normal.en: The prefix ultra- also appears in ultrasonic and ultraviolet, meaning beyond the normal range.
normal.cn: 前缀 ultra- 也出现在 ultrasonic 与 ultraviolet 中，都表示超出常规范围。

normal.en: The suffix -ness turns it into ultracleanness, the degree of being cleaned to that level.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ness 把它变成表示洁净程度的抽象名词。

normal.en: Some companies spell it with a hyphen as ultra-clean in product names.
normal.cn: 这个词还有加连字符的异拼 ultra-clean，常见于产品名，意思不变。

normal.en: In industry the setting is a cleanroom, where dust itself is the enemy.
normal.cn: 在工业语境里，它的场景是超级净间，尘埃本身就是敌人。

normal.en: Compare sterile, which kills germs, and ultraclean, which also keeps out dust and impurities.
normal.cn: 对比 sterile：sterile 针对细菌，ultraclean 连灰尘与杂质也一并挡住。

abstract.en: Picture a white air-shower gate blowing dust off a worker in a bunny suit.
abstract.cn: 想象一道白色风淋门，把穿着连体服的工人身上的灰尘吹走。

abstract.en: Think of a car burning fuel so pure that the exhaust pipe stays bright silver.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆车烧着极纯净的燃料，排气管始终亮银如新。

abstract.en: Imagine a factory whose waste pipe drips nothing at all.
abstract.cn: 想象一座工厂的排污管一滴东西都流不出来。

examples.en: Microchips are made in ultraclean rooms to keep dust off the silicon.
examples.cn: 芯片在超净间里制造，以免灰尘落到硅片上。

examples.en: The report calls for ultraclean fuel and stricter emission tests.
examples.cn: 报告要求使用超清洁燃料并加严排放检测。

examples.en: After the renovation, the lab looked ultraclean and almost empty.
examples.cn: 翻修之后，实验室看上去一尘不染，几乎空无一物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊，吹克林」——进门先被风淋一吹，把沙沙作响的尘粒全吹掉，就达到了超洁净；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ultra（越过、超出）+ 英语 clean（洁净）→ 现代复合词 ultraclean，核心义「洁净到超出常规限度」。

sensesIntro.en: Ultraclean pushes ordinary clean to an extreme: dust-free space first, then pure substances, then near-zero-waste processes, and finally an immaculate look.
sensesIntro.cn: ultraclean 把普通的「干净」推向极端：先是无尘空间，再是纯净物质，之后是近乎零废料的工艺，最后是一尘不染的外观。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white room where the air carries not a single speck.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间白色的房间，空气里连一粒尘埃都没有。

branches.en: The dust-free room is the technical core sense.
branches.cn: 无尘房间是技术上的核心义项。

branches.en: Purity of fuel or water is the material sense.
branches.cn: 燃料或水的纯净是物质层面的义项。

branches.en: Near-zero-waste production is the process sense.
branches.cn: 近乎零废料的生产是工艺层面的义项。

branches.en: A spotless surface is the everyday visual sense.
branches.cn: 一尘不染的表面是日常的视觉义项。

branches.en: All four share the same extreme of no unwanted specks or impurities.
branches.cn: 四个义项共享同一种极端：没有任何多余的微粒或杂质。

intro.en: Ultraclean is modern English built from the Latin prefix ultra- and the old Germanic word clean.
intro.cn: ultraclean 是由拉丁前缀 ultra- 与古日耳曼语词 clean 构成的现代英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ultra means beyond; its earlier form ulter means the far side, and the same family gives ulterior and ultimate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ultra 意为「越过」，更早形式 ulter 意为「彼方」，同族还有 ulterior 与 ultimate。

items.example: The prefix ultra- makes clean extreme.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ultra- 把 clean 的程度推到极致。

items.example: Ultra is the Latin source of the prefix.
items.exampleCN: ultra 是该前缀的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Clean is the English base word.
items.exampleCN: clean 是英语基本词。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms ultracleanness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 ultracleanness。

items.example: Ultracleanness is tested with particle counters.
items.exampleCN: 超洁净程度用粒子计数器检测。

items.example: Ultra-clean appears in product names.
items.exampleCN: ultra-clean 常见于产品名称。

items.example: Ultrasonic cleaning uses high-frequency waves.
items.exampleCN: 超声波清洗利用高频波。

items.example: Ultraviolet light is used to sterilise rooms.
items.exampleCN: 紫外线灯用于给房间灭菌。

items.meaning: a room with strictly controlled particles
items.example: Chip plants depend on cleanrooms.
items.exampleCN: 芯片厂离不开洁净室。

items.example: The prefix ultra- also forms ultramodern.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ultra- 也构成 ultramodern。

definition_zh: 超声；超声波；超声波检查
definition_en: sound waves with a frequency too high for people to hear, or a medical test that uses them to look inside the body
core_image: 一束高到耳朵听不见的声波射进身体，再弹回来，在屏幕上画出一幅内部图
scene: 孕检室里，医生把探头贴在肚皮上，屏幕很快显出胎儿的轮廓。The doctor used ultrasound to check how the baby was growing.
sceneCN: 这里 ultrasound 是「超声波检查」（第 4 个义项：用高频声波查看体内情况的医学检查）；句意：医生用超声波检查胎儿的生长情况。

pos.zh: 超声；超声波；超声波检查

collocations.zh: 超声波扫描；B 超检查

derivatives.zh: 由前缀 ultra- 与词根 son- 加 -ic 构成，义为「超声的、超声波的」
由 ultra-、son- 与希腊语 graphia（书写）组合，义为「超声造影术」
由 ultrasonic 加副词词尾 -ally 构成，义为「以超声方式」
由拉丁语 sonus（声音）与 -gram（记录）构成，义为「超声图」

senses.title: Sound above the hearing range
senses.definition: sound waves whose frequency is so high that human ears cannot detect them
senses.definitionCN: 频率高到人耳无法察觉的声波
senses.example: Bats hunt at night by sending out ultrasound.
senses.exampleCN: 蝙蝠在夜间发出超声波来捕食。
senses.why: Latin ultra means beyond, and sonus means sound, so ultrasound is literally sound placed beyond the reach of the ear.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ultra 意为「超出」，sonus 意为「声音」，所以 ultrasound 字面上就是「超出听力范围的声音」，词本身已经把核心意象说了出来。

senses.title: Imaging with reflected echoes
senses.definition: the technique of sending these waves into an object and building a picture from the echoes that bounce back
senses.definitionCN: 把这种声波送入物体、再靠反射回来的回声拼出画面的技术
senses.example: Ultrasound lets engineers inspect metal parts for hidden cracks.
senses.exampleCN: 超声让工程师能检查金属部件里看不见的裂纹。
senses.why: Once you know that unheard sound bounces off surfaces, the obvious next step is to listen to the echo and draw what blocked it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦知道听不见的声音碰到物体会反弹，下一步自然是去听回声，再把挡住它的东西画出来，这就是成像。

senses.title: A scanning device
senses.definition: the machine, or the hand-held probe, that produces the waves and reads the returning signals
senses.definitionCN: 产生声波并读取返回信号的机器或手持探头
senses.example: The technician wiped the gel off the ultrasound before the patient left.
senses.exampleCN: 病人离开前，技师擦掉了超声仪上的凝胶。
senses.why: Because the technique needs hardware, the word also came to name the tool, just as scanner names the machine behind a scan.
