senses.title: Not noticing what is happening
senses.definition: not noticing something that is going on close by, or that one should have noticed
senses.definitionCN: 没有注意到身边正在发生、本该注意到的事
senses.example: She was unaware of the water dripping from the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 她没注意到屋顶在漏水。
senses.why: Wær meant watchful, so aware is being on the lookout; un- removes the watchfulness and leaves a person whose eyes are somewhere else.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 wær 意为「警觉的」，aware 就是留神看着；否定前缀 un- 把这份留神拿掉，人就还在别处看着。

senses.title: Not knowing a fact
senses.definition: not having a piece of information that others may have, and not being told of it
senses.definitionCN: 没有掌握别人可能已掌握的信息，也没有被告知
senses.example: Many residents were unaware that the road would close.
senses.exampleCN: 许多居民并不知道这条路要封闭。
senses.why: Aware that introduces a known fact, so the negative says a fact has never reached this person at all.
senses.whyCN: aware that 引出一个已知事实，否定形式就表示这个事实根本没有传到当事人那里。

senses.title: Without conscious knowledge or intent
senses.definition: not aware as a state of mind, as in unaware habits, reflexes or drives that work below the surface of thought
senses.definitionCN: 指不处于意识状态，如未察觉的习惯、反射或思虑之外的冲动
senses.example: She had an unaware habit of tapping the table.
senses.exampleCN: 她有个自己没察觉的敲桌子习惯。
senses.why: The negative drops the watchful self from the act, so the person is doing something while not knowing that they do it.
senses.whyCN: 否定把「留神的自己」从动作里抽走，于是人做着某件事，却不知道自己在做。

senses.title: Left out of a decision
senses.definition: of an authority, a public or a group, kept from knowing a plan or a decision that affects it
senses.definitionCN: 指当局、公众或群体不知道与自己有关的计划或决定
senses.example: The public was unaware that the plant would be closed.
senses.exampleCN: 公众不知道这家工厂将关闭。
senses.why: Availability of information is the condition for awareness, so a sealed file leaves a whole public unaware.
senses.whyCN: 信息能不能拿到，决定人有没有意识；文件一封，整群人都处在不知情里。

senses.title: Caught by surprise
senses.definition: in the set phrase caught unaware, doing something without warning and being surprised while unprepared
senses.definitionCN: 在固定说法 catch someone unaware 中，指在毫无防备时被突然撞见或抓住
senses.example: The flood caught the village unaware at night.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水在夜里让全村措手不及。
senses.why: The fixed phrase keeps the same missing watch but fixes it to one moment: no watch was on, so the surprise lands.
senses.whyCN: 这个固定说法保留的仍是「警觉缺席」，只是把它固定在一个瞬间：当时没人留神，于是突袭正好落下。

senses.title: Untroubled by a danger
senses.definition: used with a pleasant adverb such as blissfully, of someone calmly free of worry because the danger has not reached them
senses.definitionCN: 与 blissfully 等愉快的副词连用，指因为危险还没波及而安逸、毫不在意
senses.example: The picnic went on, blissfully unaware of the storm clouds.
senses.exampleCN: 野餐照旧进行，大家对着压过来的乌云浑然不觉。
senses.why: The watch is off, and here the switch being off is a comfort rather than a fault, so the same negation reads as calm.
senses.whyCN: 警觉是关着的，只是这一次关着反而让人舒服，同一个否定就读成了安逸。

senses.title: Failing to notice a fault
senses.definition: in criticism, of a person who does not see their own weakness or bias even when others can
senses.definitionCN: 在评论中，指当事人看不出自身的弱点或偏见，而别人却看得清楚
senses.example: Unaware of his own accent, he corrected everyone else.
senses.exampleCN: 他对自己口音的毛病毫无察觉，却去纠正别人。
senses.why: The watchful sense turns inward as well, and an inward watch that fails is the blind spot a critic names.
senses.whyCN: 警觉的目光也照向自己，照向自己的那束光一旦失灵，就是评论者所说的盲点。

senses.title: Uninformed by the data
senses.definition: of an estimate, a policy or a judgement, made without knowledge of the relevant facts
senses.definitionCN: 指估计、政策或判断是在不了解相关事实的情况下作出的
senses.example: Unaware estimates of the loss were far too low.
senses.exampleCN: 不了解实情时作出的损失估计远远偏低。
senses.why: When the watch was never given the facts, the judgement built on it inherits the same blindness.
senses.whyCN: 警觉从头到尾没拿到事实，建在它上面的判断于是也一并瞎了。

intro.en: Unaware is a two-brick word: the Old English watchful root wær sits under the native prefix un-, and the spelling aware was reshaped to match ware.
intro.cn: unaware 由两块材料拼成：底层是古英语表示「警觉」的词根 wær，前面是本土否定前缀 un-；中间 a- 的拼写还受过 ware（当心）的影响。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to watch or to guard lies behind the family, and it also gives ward, warn and wary.
items.cn: 一个意为「看守、注意」的重构词根支撑这一族词，ward、warn、wary 都出自它。

items.en: Wær meant watchful or cautious, and the compound gewær meant aware of something.
items.cn: wær 意为警觉、谨慎，复合形式 gewær 表示觉察到某事。

items.en: The prefix be- joined the root to make the warning formula beware, Be thou aware.
items.cn: 前缀 be- 与词根结合成警告用语 beware，原义是「你要小心」。

items.en: The a- prefix form grew beside ware, and in the North and in Scotland it became aware.
items.cn: a- 前缀形式与 ware 并存，在英格兰北部与苏格兰发展为 aware。

items.en: Aware settled into general use, and the native negator un- gave unaware its opposite.
items.cn: aware 进入通行用法，本土否定前缀 un- 给出反义形式 unaware。

items.en: The fixed phrases unaware of, unaware that and caught unaware now carry almost all of its public use.
items.cn: 如今它的公开用法几乎都由固定说法 unaware of、unaware that 与 caught unaware 承担。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same watchful root and on the same native prefix; the near-meaning group gathers neighbours of knowing and, at the end, the plain opposite.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「警觉」词根与同一本土前缀构成的词；近义组收与「知情」相邻的说法，最后收一个直接的反义词。

entries.definition: Knowing, noticing or being alert to something; the positive word that un- turns into the opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 指知道的、察觉到的，是本词去掉否定前缀后的肯定形式。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning suddenly, without warning, or without being noticed.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「出其不意地、冷不防地」。

entries.definition: To be careful of a danger; the prefix be- plus the watchful root lies behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 指当心危险；由前缀 be- 与「警觉」词根构成。

entries.definition: Careful and watchful about possible trouble; the adjective of the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 指谨慎提防的，是同一词根的形容词。

entries.definition: Not at ease, slightly worried; it shares the un- shape but comes from ease, not from the watchful root.
entries.definitionCN: 指不安的、有点担心的；同样带否定前缀，但词根是 ease，只是构词外形相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Lacking knowledge, often of whole subjects, and frequently used as a blunt criticism.
entries.definitionCN: 指缺乏知识，常指对整类事物不了解，语气往往带有责难。

entries.definition: Completely not noticing something, so that it cannot affect attention at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指完全没注意到，以至于对方根本影响不到注意力。

entries.definition: Not having received the facts that others have, mostly said of judgement or opinion.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有获得别人已掌握的实情，多形容判断或意见。

entries.definition: In a sleep or faint state, or having a reaction without deciding on it.
entries.definitionCN: 指昏迷或睡着，也指没经过决定就产生的反应。

entries.definition: Awake to something and deliberately noticing it; the most direct contrary of the word.
entries.definitionCN: 指清醒地认识到某事并刻意留心，是本词最直接的反义说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English watchful root, the native negator and the phrases this word actually forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语「警觉」词根、本土否定成分，以及这个词实际构成的搭配。

normal.en: The root wær is watchful, so unaware is a watch that has been switched off.
normal.cn: 词根 wær 是「警觉」，所以 unaware 就是被关掉的警觉。

normal.en: Beware and wary come from the same root: one says be watchful, the other says watchful.
normal.cn: beware 与 wary 同出这个词根：一个叫你留心，一个形容留心。

normal.en: The usual patterns are unaware of plus a noun and unaware that plus a clause.
normal.cn: 常见结构是 unaware 后接介词加名词，或接 that 从句。

normal.en: Blissfully unaware is a gentle joke: the trouble is real, the person simply has not met it yet.
normal.cn: 浑然不知是一种温和的玩笑：麻烦是真的，只是人还没遇上。

normal.en: Compare conscious and oblivious: unaware sits between the mild and the total.
normal.cn: 对比 conscious 与 oblivious：unaware 正好落在「稍有察觉」与「全无察觉」之间。

abstract.en: Picture a torch lowered toward the pavement: the rain has stopped behind you, but the beam never swings back.
abstract.cn: 想象手电筒的光只照向地面：雨在身后停了，那束光却从不回头。

abstract.en: An unaware person is not foolish; the information simply never arrived at the door where they were standing.
abstract.cn: 未被察觉不是愚蠢，只是信息从未送到人所站的那扇门前。

abstract.en: The word is a report about a gap, not an accusation about a character.
abstract.cn: 这个词报告的是一道缺口，而不是对人品的指责。

examples.en: He was unaware of the debt until the letter arrived.
examples.cn: 信寄到之前，他一直不知道有这笔欠款。

examples.en: The children played on, unaware that the tide had turned.
examples.cn: 孩子们继续玩耍，不知道潮水已经转向。

examples.en: Unaware of the change, she turned up an hour early.
examples.cn: 她不知道有变动，提前一小时就到了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「安呐威尔」——「安呐」坐着安稳，外面发生了什么一概不问：没察觉到、不知道；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 否定前缀 un-（不）+ aware；aware 出自古英语 wær「警觉的、谨慎的」及复合形式 gewær「觉察到的」，属日耳曼语系，同族有 beware、wary、ward，更早的原始印欧语词根属重构形式；前置 a- 受 ware（当心）拼写影响，词源上与 ware 无关。首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all remove the watchful eye: not noticing, not knowing a fact, acting without knowing it, kept in the dark, caught off guard, untroubled by danger, blind to one own fault, and proceeding without the facts.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在拿掉那只留神的眼睛：没察觉、不知道事实、自己不知道自己在做、被蒙在鼓里、措手不及、对着危险浑然不觉、看不见自己的毛病，以及不掌握情况的判断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a passer-by looks at a phone, lifts a shoe out of a puddle, and only then sees that the rain has stopped.
core.cn: 核心意象：行人看着手机，从水洼里抬起鞋来，才发现雨早已停了。

branches.en: THE EYE: the gaze is elsewhere, so a change nearby and even ones own habit go unseen.
branches.cn: 眼睛线：目光在别处，所以身边的变化，甚至自己的习惯都没看见。

branches.en: THE MESSAGE: a fact or a plan is never delivered, so whole groups stand outside it.
branches.cn: 消息线：事实或计划从未送达，于是整群人都站在消息之外。

branches.en: THE TRAP: the word of warning does not arrive, and the surprise comes in the dark.
branches.cn: 陷阱线：警告没送到，突袭在黑夜里发生。

branches.en: THE CALM: ignorance here is oddly peaceful, because the danger has not touched the picnic yet.
branches.cn: 安逸线：此处的不知情反而安宁，因为危险还没碰到那场野餐。

branches.en: THE MIRROR AND THE FILE: an inward watch that fails, and a judgement made without the papers.
branches.cn: 镜子与卷宗线：照向自己的警觉失灵，以及没拿到卷宗就下的判断。

intro.en: Unaware is a native prefix plus a native root, with no Latin parts at all, which is why the whole watchful family feels so much like English.
intro.cn: unaware 是本土前缀加本土词根，不含任何拉丁成分，所以这一整族「警觉」词读起来特别像英语自己的词。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin ancestor; the modern Latin spellings listed here are later learned words, kept only to show how the same idea was borrowed and reshaped.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源；这里列的现代拉丁式拼写都是后来借用的书面词形，只为说明同一语义如何被借去改造。

items.example: The native prefix turns aware into unaware.
items.exampleCN: 这个本土前缀把 aware 变成 unaware。

items.example: Wær is the watchful root of the family.
items.exampleCN: wær 是这一族词表示警觉的词根。

items.example: The compound carried the prefix ge-.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合形式带前缀 ge-。

items.meaningCN: 介词 on 的弱化形式
items.example: The prefix appears in the spelling aware.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀出现在 aware 的拼写上。

items.example: Aware is the base of the negative.
items.exampleCN: aware 是否定形式的底座。

items.example: Unaware names the missing watch.
items.exampleCN: unaware 指缺了的那份留神。

items.example: The suffix forms unawareness.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 unawareness。

items.example: The suffix appears in the adverb unawares.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀出现在副词 unawares 里。

items.example: Beware joins the prefix and the watchful root.
items.exampleCN: beware 由该前缀与「警觉」词根结合而成。

items.example: Wary keeps the watchful sense alive.
items.exampleCN: wary 让「警觉」这个意思留在日常里。

definition_zh: 无敌的；打不赢的；极好的；无与伦比的；（物价）极优的
definition_en: too strong or good to be beaten, defeated or improved upon, whether in a contest, at a price or in quality
core_image: 棋桌对面的人已经起身，棋盘上自己这方一枚子都没少
scene: 棋局还没下到最后，对面那位已经起身收起水杯，棋盘上这边一枚子都没少。At this level she is unbeatable on the clay courts.
sceneCN: 这里 unbeatable 是「打不赢、无敌」（第 1 个义项：在比赛或较量中不会输）；句意是在这个级别上，她在红土球场上无人能胜。画面里对面起身收杯的动作，比比分更能说明「打不了」。

pos.zh: 形容词：无敌的；打不赢的；极好的

forms.label: 比较级（用 more 构成）
最高级（用 most 构成）
肯定形式（去掉否定前缀）

derivatives.zh: 该词去掉否定前缀后的肯定形容词，义为「可被打败的」；通常用于 one is beatable 这样的短句
由动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「搅拌器；打猎时驱赶猎物的人」
由动词加动名词尾构成，义为「痛打；惨败」
由同一词根加过去分词尾构成，义为「未被击败的」；侧重战绩记录，与本词侧重不可战胜不同

senses.title: Too strong to lose
senses.definition: of a player, a team or a side in a contest, so strong that beating them is beyond reach
senses.definitionCN: 指比赛中的选手、球队或一方实力太强，对手根本打不赢
senses.example: At home the team has been unbeatable for a season.
senses.exampleCN: 整个赛季里，这支队伍在主场无人能胜。
senses.why: Beat is the plainest English verb for striking a blow and winning, and -able adds can be, so un- plus that gives cannot be beaten.
senses.whyCN: beat 是英语里最朴素的「打、赢」动词，-able 表示「可以被……」，前面再加否定前缀就成了「不可能被打败」。

senses.title: Beyond improvement
senses.titleCN: 无可超越的；无与伦比的
senses.definition: of a quality, a performance or a record, so excellent that nothing can do better
senses.definitionCN: 指品质、表现或纪录好到无法再被超越
senses.example: Her timing on the final swim was unbeatable.
senses.exampleCN: 她在最后一泳的节奏无可超越。
senses.why: Beating someone also means bettering them, so a performance that cannot be bettered is unbeatable in the evaluative sense.
senses.whyCN: beat 除了「打败」，还有「胜过」的意思，所以无法被胜过的东西就是无可超越的。

senses.title: The best value on offer
senses.definition: of a price, a deal or a combination, so good that no other offer can undercut it
senses.definitionCN: 指价格、交易或搭配好到没有别家能压得更低
senses.example: Two tickets for the price of one is an unbeatable offer.
senses.exampleCN: 一张票的钱买两张，这个优惠无可匹敌。
senses.why: On shop signs the contest becomes a market, and a rival price that cannot beat yours makes your price unbeatable.
senses.whyCN: 招牌上的较量变成了市场：对手的价格压不过你，你的价格就成了无可匹敌。

senses.title: Hard to argue against
senses.titleCN: 无可辩驳的；无法反驳的
senses.definition: of a case, an argument or an excuse, so strong that it succeeds against every objection
senses.definitionCN: 指理由、论证或借口太强，任何反驳都站不住
senses.example: A doctor note is an unbeatable excuse for missing class.
senses.exampleCN: 有病假条，缺课的理由就无从辩驳。
senses.why: Debate is a contest in which one side wins, and an argument that wins every time is unbeatable.
senses.whyCN: 辩论本身就是一场有胜负的较量，每次都能赢下的理由自然不可战胜。

senses.title: Impossible to overcome
senses.definition: of a difficulty, an obstacle or an opponent like illness, so severe that no effort gets past it
senses.definitionCN: 指困难、障碍或像疾病这样的对手严重到怎么努力都过不去
senses.example: The heat made the last climb unbeatable that day.
senses.exampleCN: 那天的高温让最后一段爬坡怎么也过不去。
senses.why: Here the thing to be beaten is not a rival but a condition that wins the round, and the same verb of winning is simply reversed.
senses.whyCN: 这里的对手不是人，而是赢得这一回合的条件，用的仍是同一个「胜负」动词，只是方向反过来。

senses.title: Too attractive to resist
senses.definition: of a proposal, an invitation or an appeal, so attractive that no one can turn it down
senses.definitionCN: 指提议、邀约或吸引力大到没人拒绝得掉
senses.example: A paid year in another country was an unbeatable chance.
senses.exampleCN: 带薪在外国待一年，这个机会让人无法拒绝。
senses.why: A temptation that wins against your resistance is beating you, so an appeal that cannot be turned down is unbeatable.
senses.whyCN: 抵不过的诱惑其实就是在「打败」你，所以无法拒绝的吸引力同样不可战胜。

senses.title: Dependable in practice
senses.definition: of a habit, a method or a tool, so reliable under pressure that it never lets you down
senses.definitionCN: 指习惯、办法或工具可靠到关键时刻从不失手
senses.example: For heavy rain, a good pair of boots is unbeatable.
senses.exampleCN: 遇上大雨，一双好靴子是无敌的。
senses.why: Reliability is measured in contests with the weather and the clock, and whatever wins those small contests is unbeatable.
senses.whyCN: 可靠与否要在与天气、时间的较量中检验，凡能赢下这些小较量的东西就是无敌的。

senses.title: Hitting the mark with charm
senses.definition: in relaxed speech, used loosely of a joke, a dish or a moment that could hardly be bettered
senses.definitionCN: 口语中宽泛地指笑话、菜或某个时刻好得不能再好
senses.example: That closing joke was unbeatable.
senses.exampleCN: 那个收尾的笑话真是绝了。
senses.why: Loose praise borrows the contest image from games: the moment wins over every other version of itself.
senses.whyCN: 轻松的赞美借用了竞技的画面：这个时刻胜过它自己的所有其他版本。

intro.en: Unbeatable is a thoroughly English word: an English verb, an English suffix and an English negative, with no Latin root behind it at all.
intro.cn: unbeatable 是个纯英语构造的词：英语动词、英语后缀、英语否定成分，背后没有拉丁词根。

items.en: A reconstructed verb meaning to strike or to hammer, the source of the English beat, is the deepest layer.
items.cn: 最深一层是一个重构的日耳曼语动词，意为「击打、锤打」，英语 beat 由此而来。

items.en: Bēatan meant to beat or strike, and it already covered striking metal into shape.
items.cn: bēatan 意为击打，当时已经包含把金属敲打成形的意思。

items.en: The verb kept the striking sense and grew the senses of defeating a rival and of surpassing a mark.
items.cn: 这个动词保留了击打义，又长出「击败对手」与「超过某个刻度」的意思。

items.en: The suffix -able turned verbs into adjectives of possibility, giving beatable alongside many others.
items.cn: 后缀 -able 把动词变成表示「可能」的形容词，beatable 就是其中一员。

items.en: The native negator un- was fixed in front of the whole adjective, so the denial covers cannot be beaten rather than simply not beatable.
items.cn: 本土否定成分 un- 加在整个形容词前面，所以否定覆盖的是「不可能被打败」，而不只是「没被击败」。

items.en: Advertising gave the word its price sense, and this shape of negated -able adjective is still being coined today; the exact date of unbeatable is uncertain.
items.cn: 广告给了它报价的义项；这种「否定前缀 + 动词 + 后缀」的形容词今天仍在不断造新，unbeatable 的确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other words built from the same striking verb and the same negative prefix; the near-meaning group gathers neighbours of winning and of being best, with the plain opposite last.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「击打」动词与同一否定前缀构成的词；近义组收与「取胜、最好」相邻的说法，最后放一个直接的反义词。

entries.definition: Not yet defeated, a record kept clean so far; it tells you about the past, not about whether a loss is possible.
entries.definitionCN: 指至今未被击败、战绩干净；它说的是过去的记录，不说今后是否可能输。

entries.definition: Able to be beaten, the positive word that un- turns into its opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 指可以被打败的，是本词去掉否定前缀后的肯定形式。

entries.definition: A tool that beats, such as an egg beater, or a person who drives game out of cover.
entries.definitionCN: 指击打用的工具，如打蛋器，或把猎物赶出藏身处的人。

entries.definition: Too painful to put up with; it shares the un- plus -able shape but comes from bear, and only looks like the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 指难以忍受的；同样由否定前缀加 -able 构成，但词根是 bear，只是构词外形相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A fight between armed forces; it is sometimes felt to belong with beat, but it comes through Old French from a different battle term.
entries.definitionCN: 指武装力量之间的战斗；常被认为与 beat 同族，实际经古法语来自另一个表示「战斗」的说法，词源不同。

entries.definition: Formal and grand, of a power or force that cannot be conquered by any enemy.
entries.definitionCN: 正式而宏大，指任何对手都无法征服的力量。

entries.definition: Very close in meaning but much rarer, with a longer and heavier sound.
entries.definitionCN: 意思与本词极近，但远为罕用，读音也更长更重。

entries.definition: Having no equal at all, a literary word about quality rather than about contests.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有任何匹敌者，是书面语，谈的是品质而非比赛。

entries.definition: Without a peer or an equal, the formal register of praising someone outstanding.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有同等者，是称赞卓越者的正式说法。

entries.definition: Able to be defeated, so it puts a plain doubt on any talk of an unbeatable side.
entries.definitionCN: 指可以被打败的，一听这个词，任何「无敌」的说法都带着疑问。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real striking verb, the productive suffix pair and the shop phrases this word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的「击打」动词、成词能力很强的后缀组合，以及这个词实际出现的商业搭配。

normal.en: Beat gives beating, beaten and beatable, so the word is simply the verb wearing a long suffix coat.
normal.cn: beat 能变出 beating、beaten、beatable，这个词不过是给动词披上一件长后缀外衣。

normal.en: Unbeaten and unbeatable are cousins: unbeaten looks back at the record, unbeatable looks forward at the next match.
normal.cn: unbeaten 与 unbeatable 是表亲：前者回看战绩，后者前瞻下一场。

normal.en: The same -able pattern gives breakable, beatable and washable, all of them built from plain English verbs.
normal.cn: 同样的 -able 模式还能造出 breakable、beatable、washable，全都由朴素的英语动词构成。

normal.en: On a price ticket, low unbeatable price simply means nobody can undercut you today.
normal.cn: 在价格牌上，最低价、无可匹敌的说法，不过是说今天没人能压得更低。

normal.en: Compare unbearable: one letter pair between a word about winning and a word about patience.
normal.cn: 对比 unbearable：赢家的词与忍耐的词之间只差一两笔。

abstract.en: Picture the empty chair opposite you: the strongest sign of winning is that the opponent has stopped playing.
abstract.cn: 想象对面那把空椅子：赢最有力的证据，是对手不再下了。

abstract.en: Every sense keeps a scale: a score, a price, a standard, a hardship, and unbeatable means the scale cannot go past it.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都守着一把尺子：比分、价格、标准、困境，而不可战胜就是说这把尺子再也上不去。

abstract.en: The word is praise built from fighting vocabulary, which is why advertisers love it and sports reporters use it with care.
abstract.cn: 这个词是用打斗词汇搭出的赞美，所以广告爱用它，体育记者却用得谨慎。

examples.en: The shop offers an unbeatable price on winter coats.
examples.cn: 这家店冬季大衣的价格无可匹敌。

examples.en: No side is truly unbeatable, whatever the supporters say.
examples.cn: 无论球迷怎么说，没有哪支队伍真正无敌。

examples.en: A hot bath and a long sleep proved an unbeatable cure for the cold.
examples.cn: 热水澡加长睡一觉，治这场感冒再好不过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读起来像「安必特」——「安」稳得「必」定「特」别难打发：无敌的、打不赢的；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 否定前缀 un-（不）+ beat + -able（可以……的）；beat 出自古英语 bēatan「击打」，属日耳曼语系，更早的原始日耳曼语形式属重构；由「打击」引申为「击败、胜过」，整词即「不可能被击败」。全部构词成分都是英语本土成分，没有拉丁词根，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep the same contest: a rival, a rival mark, a competitor price, an opposing argument, a hardship, an urge to refuse, the weather, and other versions of the same moment.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项守的都是同一场较量：对手、对手的纪录、对手的报价、对方的论证、困境、想拒绝的冲动、天气，以及同一个时刻的其他版本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty chair across the chessboard, and every piece on your side still standing.
core.cn: 核心意象：棋盘对面那把椅子空了，自己这方的棋子一枚没少。

branches.en: THE CONTEST: the oldest line, where a side simply cannot be beaten on the field.
branches.cn: 赛场线：最古老的一条，赛场上一方根本赢不了。

branches.en: THE SCALE: a mark that cannot be outdone and a price no rival can undercut.
branches.cn: 刻度线：再也超不过的纪录，以及没人压得下去的报价。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT: a case that wins every round, and a hardship that wins over every effort.
branches.cn: 论证线：每回合都赢的理由，以及压过一切努力的困境。

branches.en: THE PULL: an appeal that beats your resistance, and a tool that beats the weather.
branches.cn: 拉力线：抵过你抗拒的吸引力，以及胜过天气的可靠工具。

branches.en: THE CHAT: the looseness of praise, where the contest has shrunk to a joke or a dish.
branches.cn: 闲聊线：赞美变得松散，较量的对象缩成了笑话或一道菜。

intro.en: Unbeatable shows one of the most productive English patterns: a negative prefix, a plain verb and the suffix -able, layered in that order.
intro.cn: unbeatable 展示了英语最能产的构词模式之一：否定前缀、简单动词再加后缀 -able，一层层叠上去。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor here, since beat is Old English; the Latin forms listed are later borrowings that were never part of this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源，因为 beat 出自古英语；所列的拉丁形式都是后来借入的其他词，从未参与本词的构成。

items.example: The native prefix turns beatable into its opposite.
items.exampleCN: 这个本土前缀把 beatable 翻成反义。

items.example: The verb supplies both the hitting and the winning sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词同时提供「击打」与「取胜」两层意思。

items.example: The suffix forms beatable from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成 beatable。

items.example: Beatable is the base of the negative.
items.exampleCN: beatable 是否定形式的底座。

items.example: Unbeatable names the impossible loss.
items.exampleCN: unbeatable 指输不掉的状态。

items.example: The suffix forms unbeaten from the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成本词的近亲 unbeaten。

items.example: The suffix gives beater.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 beater。

items.example: The suffix gives beating.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 beating。

items.example: Bēatan already struck metal into shape.
items.exampleCN: bēatan 当时已指把金属敲打成器形。

definition_zh: 不合适的；不得体的；不相称的；降低身份的
definition_en: not suitable or proper for someone in a particular situation, especially in a way that seems rude or makes them lose respect
core_image: 一件尺寸和身份都不搭的外套，穿在身上显得别扭
scene: 一位受人尊敬的老师在同事面前大声抱怨、摔门而去，事后有人说，这样的举动与他的身份实在不相称，有失体面。Losing your temper in the staffroom is unbecoming of a senior teacher.
sceneCN: 这里 unbecoming 是「不得体的、有失身份的」（第 1 个义项：与身份或身份场合不相称）；句意：在教师办公室里发脾气，对一位资深教师来说是有失体面的。

pos.zh: 不得体的；与身份不相称的

collocations.zh: 对某人来说不成体统的

forms.label: 作表语（接 of 或 to）

derivatives.zh: 不得体地；不相称地
不得体；不相称
得体的；相称的；合适的
适合；与……相称
不适合的；不称职的（否定前缀加词根的平行构词）

senses.title: Not fitting a person or a role
senses.titleCN: 与身份不相称的；有失体面的
senses.definition: not suitable for a person or position, usually because it damages their dignity or reputation
senses.definitionCN: 不适合某个人或某个职位，通常因为损害了其尊严或声誉
senses.example: Losing your temper in public is unbecoming of a head teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 在公共场合发脾气，对一位校长来说是有失体面的。
senses.why: The un- prefix simply denies, and become here carries the older sense of fitting or befitting, so unbecoming says that something does not fit a person.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 只是否定，而此处的 become 保留了「适合、配得上」的旧义，所以 unbecoming 说的就是与某人不搭、不合身分。

senses.title: Not suitable for an occasion
senses.definition: unsuitable or improper for a particular situation, place, or occasion
senses.definitionCN: 对特定情境、场合或氛围而言不合适或不恰当
senses.example: Bright jeans are unbecoming for a formal ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 亮色牛仔裤在正式仪式上是不合场合的。
senses.why: Once the word means not fitting a person, it easily extends to things that do not fit the moment, such as clothes or remarks.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词表示与人不相称，自然就扩展到与场合不相称的东西，比如衣着或言辞。

senses.title: Rude or embarrassing
senses.definition: behaving in a way that seems rude, tasteless, or makes other people uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 行为粗鲁、缺乏品味或让旁人感到不舒服
senses.example: Loud jokes at a funeral feel unbecoming.
senses.exampleCN: 葬礼上大声说笑令人觉得失礼。
senses.why: What does not fit a situation usually offends those present, so the word takes on a tone of social disapproval.
senses.whyCN: 不合场合的行为往往会冒犯在场的人，于是这个词带上了旁人皱眉、社会不认可的意味，表示失礼。

senses.title: Unflattering in appearance
senses.definition: used about clothes or colours that do not look flattering on the wearer
senses.definitionCN: 指衣物或颜色穿在某人身上不显好看
senses.example: That dull grey shade is rather unbecoming on her.
senses.exampleCN: 那种暗淡的灰色穿在她身上显不出好看。
senses.why: The fitting image moves from manners to the body, so a dress can be unbecoming when it does not suit the person wearing it.
senses.whyCN: 「合身与否」的意象从举止转到身形，衣服不合人时就可以说它 unbecoming，即不衬这个人。

senses.title: Lowering in status
senses.titleCN: 降低身份的；有失身份的
senses.definition: used to say that a job or act is below what someone s rank or position deserves
senses.definitionCN: 表示某项工作或行为低于某人身份所应有的水平
senses.example: Cleaning the toilets with the caretaker seemed unbecoming to the new manager.
senses.exampleCN: 跟管理员一起刷厕所，对新任经理来说似乎有失身份。
senses.why: The sense of role and rank inside become grows visible here, and the word quietly accuses the task of dragging the person down.
senses.whyCN: become 里「角色与地位」的含义在这里浮现出来，这个词在暗示这项活儿把人拉低了身价。

intro.en: Unbecoming is the negative of becoming in the old verbal sense of befitting, so it literally says that something does not become a person.
intro.cn: unbecoming 是 becoming 在「适合」这一古老动词意义上的否定形式，字面意思就是「不适合某人」。

items.en: Becuman means to come to be, from be- and cuman, to come.
items.cn: 古英语 becuman 意为「出现、成为」，由 be- 与 cuman（来）构成。

items.en: Bicumen adds the sense of befitting someone or something.
items.cn: 中古英语 bicumen 加入了「与……相称」的意思。

items.en: Becoming is used as an adjective meaning fitting and graceful.
items.cn: becoming 被用作形容词，表示合适、得体。

items.en: The negative unbecoming appears meaning unsuitable and improper.
items.cn: 否定形式 unbecoming 出现，表示不合适、不得体。

items.en: The word stays formal and is common in conduct unbecoming of an officer.
items.cn: 这个词保持正式色彩，常见于「有损军官身份的品行」一类说法。

note.en: Unbecoming sits between words of fitting, such as becoming and suitable, and words of taste, such as improper and indecent.
note.cn: unbecoming 位于 becoming、suitable 这类「相称」词与 improper、indecent 这类「得体」词之间。

entries.definition: suitable and attractive for a person
entries.definitionCN: 合适的；得体的；相称的

entries.definition: in an unsuitable or improper manner
entries.definitionCN: 不得体地；不相称地

entries.definition: not appropriate for a person or situation
entries.definitionCN: 不合适的；不相称的（结构相似，词根不同）

entries.definition: not correct or acceptable by social standards
entries.definitionCN: 不合适的；不合礼仪的

entries.definition: morally offensive or shocking
entries.definitionCN: 不雅的；有伤风化的

entries.definition: not suitable for the situation
entries.definitionCN: 不恰当的；不合时宜的

normalIntro.en: Unbecoming is a shirt that does not fit the body it is meant for.
normalIntro.cn: unbecoming 是一件不合身的外套，穿在原定的那个人身上显得别扭。

normal.en: Becoming means fitting and graceful, so unbecoming is its exact opposite.
normal.cn: becoming 表示合适体面，所以 unbecoming 正是它的反面。

normal.en: Becoming to someone is the old sense of suiting them, and unbecoming keeps it.
normal.cn: becoming to 某人保留了「适合某人」的古义，unbecoming 也沿用了这一结构。

normal.en: Legal and military texts say conduct unbecoming an officer.
normal.cn: 法律和军规文本常说「有损军官身份的品行」。

normal.en: The word is formal, so it suits written reports more than daily chat.
normal.cn: 这个词比较正式，更适合书面报告而不是日常闲聊。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with un-becoming, which would suggest a person is not changing.
normal.cn: 不要误读成 un 加 be 加 coming 的组合，那样会理解成「没有在变化」。

abstract.en: See a judge turning up to court in beach shorts.
abstract.cn: 想象一位法官穿着沙滩短裤走进法庭。

abstract.en: See a guest shouting at a wedding toast.
abstract.cn: 想象婚礼祝酒时一位宾客突然大喊大叫。

abstract.en: See a smart coat that is two sizes too small.
abstract.cn: 想象一件体面的外套，却小了两个码。

examples.en: Loud jokes at a funeral are unbecoming.
examples.cn: 葬礼上大声说笑是不合场合的。

examples.en: The committee said the remark was unbecoming of a senior official.
examples.cn: 委员会称这番言论有失一位高级官员的身份。

examples.en: That dull colour is unbecoming on her.
examples.cn: 那种暗淡的颜色穿在她身上不衬她。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安比卡明」——脑子里先浮现一个「安」分的人，再想他忽「比」平时更显眼，「卡」在别人的目光里，这样的样子不合身、不得体；这只是拆词的谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 becuman（出现、成为，be- + cuman 来）→ 中古英语加入「与……相称」义 → 形容词 becoming（得体的）→ un- + becoming → unbecoming（不相称的）。核心义「不适合、配不上某人」。

sensesIntro.en: Unbecoming starts with what does not fit a person, widens to what does not fit a moment, and finally drifts to clothes that do not flatter the body.
sensesIntro.cn: unbecoming 先指与人身份不相称，再扩展到与场合不相称，最后转到衣服不衬人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coat that does not fit the body it is meant for.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件不合身的外套，穿在它本该服务的那个人身上。

branches.en: What does not fit a person or role is the first sense.
branches.cn: 与个人或职位不相称，是第一个义项。

branches.en: What does not fit an occasion is the situational sense.
branches.cn: 与场合不相称，是场合义项。

branches.en: Rude or embarrassing conduct is the social sense.
branches.cn: 失礼、令人尴尬的行为，是社会评价义项。

branches.en: Clothes that do not flatter carry the fitting image onto the body.
branches.cn: 衣服不衬人，把「合身」意象用到了身体上。

branches.en: Both dignity and rank show that something is below the person.
branches.cn: 尊严与地位都说明某件事低于此人应有的水平。

intro.en: Unbecoming is built from the negative prefix un-, the verb become in its old sense of befitting, and the participle ending -ing.
intro.cn: unbecoming 由否定前缀 un-、表示「适合」的旧义词 become 和现在分词结尾 -ing 构成。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic in origin, but the prefix un- shares a distant Indo-European ancestor with Latin in- and Greek a-, both meaning not.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源于日耳曼语，但前缀 un- 与拉丁语 in-、希腊语 a- 同出一源，都表示「不」。

items.example: The prefix un- turns becoming into unbecoming.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 把 becoming 变成 unbecoming。

items.example: The prefix be- helps to build becuman.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 be- 参与构成 becuman。

items.example: The verb come comes from Old English cuman.
items.exampleCN: 动词 come 来自古英语 cuman。

items.meaning: to begin to be, or to suit
items.example: Become carries the sense that keeps unbecoming alive.
items.exampleCN: become 承载着让 unbecoming 成立的那个「适合」义。

items.example: The suffix -ing turns become into becoming.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 把 become 变成 becoming。

items.example: Becoming describes what suits a person.
items.exampleCN: becoming 描述适合某人的事物。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms unbecomingly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 unbecomingly。

items.example: Unbecomingly is the adverb of the family.
items.exampleCN: unbecomingly 是这个词族的副词。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms unbecomingness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 unbecomingness。

items.example: Unbecomingness names the quality behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: unbecomingness 指形容词背后的性质。

latinEntries.example: Latin in- is a distant relative of English un-.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 in- 与英语 un- 远古同源。

latinEntries.example: Improprius means the opposite of proper.
latinEntries.exampleCN: improprius 意为 proper 的反面。

definition_zh: 无瑕疵的；完美无缺的；洁白无损的；无污点的
definition_en: not spoiled or damaged in any way, so that it looks or remains completely perfect and pure
core_image: 一只光洁无痕的苹果，表皮上连一道擦伤都没有
scene: 一只刚摘下的苹果摆在案上，果皮光洁，没有哪怕一道划痕。She picked out an unblemished apple and polished it on her sleeve.
sceneCN: 这里 unblemished 是「无瑕疵的」（第 1 个义项：没有擦痕、斑点或损伤）；句意：她挑了一只光滑无损的苹果，用袖子把它擦了擦。

pos.zh: 无瑕疵的；洁白无损的；无污点的

derivatives.zh: 瑕疵；斑点；污点
损害；玷污
有瑕疵的；有污点的
无瑕；纯洁

senses.title: Free from physical marks
senses.definition: having no mark, spot, or damage on the surface
senses.definitionCN: 表面没有任何痕迹、斑点或损伤
senses.example: The plate was old but unblemished.
senses.exampleCN: 这只盘子虽旧，却光洁无损。
senses.why: The un- prefix denies, and blemish means a mark that spoils a surface, so the word first describes things that still look perfectly clean.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 表否定，blemish 指破坏表面的痕迹，所以这个词首先形容看起来依然完美光洁的东西。

senses.title: Free from a bad record
senses.definition: having no fault, criticism, or wrongdoing on a person s record
senses.definitionCN: 个人记录上没有任何过错、批评或不当行为
senses.example: She retired with an unblemished record.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着清白无瑕的记录退休了。
senses.why: A record is treated like a surface, and any mistake leaves a mark on it, so a clean record becomes an unblemished one.
senses.whyCN: 人们把记录看作一个表面，任何过错都会在上面留下痕迹，所以干净的记录就叫 unblemished。

senses.title: Pure and uncriticised
senses.titleCN: 纯洁无瑕的；未受指摘的
senses.definition: describing a reputation, name, or point of view that has never been attacked or accused
senses.definitionCN: 形容名声、名誉或立场从未受到攻击或指责
senses.example: His reputation remained unblemished after the inquiry.
senses.exampleCN: 调查之后，他的名声依旧未受玷污。
senses.why: Because marks suggest shame, the denied mark turns into praise for moral purity.
senses.whyCN: 因为痕迹常意味着羞耻，被否定的痕迹就转成了道德纯洁的赞语。

senses.title: Perfect in quality
senses.titleCN: 完美无缺的；无可挑剔的
senses.definition: so good that it has no visible fault at all
senses.definitionCN: 好到看不出任何缺点
senses.example: The young player had an unblemished run of wins.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻选手取得了一连串完美无缺的胜利。
senses.why: When nothing spoils the surface, the whole thing is judged flawless, and the word becomes a general term of highest praise.
senses.whyCN: 当表面上没有任何东西破坏，整件事就被判为毫无瑕疵，这个词也就成了最高级的赞美。

intro.en: Unblemished joins the negative prefix un- to blemished, the participle of blemish, a word whose deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: unblemished 由否定前缀 un- 与 blemished 相加而成，后者是 blemish 的分词形式，而 blemish 更深层的来源不确定。

items.en: The verb ble(s)mir, meaning to make pale, is proposed as a source but the link is disputed.
items.cn: 动词 ble(s)mir（使变苍白）被认为是可能的来源，但这一联系有争议。

items.en: The verb blemischen appears meaning to damage a surface.
items.cn: 中古英语动词 blemischen 出现，意为损坏表面。

items.en: The noun blemish is recorded meaning a mark that spoils something.
items.cn: 名词 blemish 见于记载，意为损坏某物的痕迹。

items.en: The participle unblemished comes into use, usually of skin and records.
items.cn: 分词形式 unblemished 开始使用，多修饰皮肤与记录。

items.en: The word is common in hospitality and sport for a clean record.
items.cn: 如今这个词常见于酒店服务与体育报道，指清白的记录。

note.en: Unblemished pairs the blemish family with words of purity, such as flawless and spotless.
note.cn: unblemished 把 blemish 词族与 flawless、spotless 这类「纯净」词并列在一起。

entries.definition: a mark that spoils the appearance of something
entries.definitionCN: 损害外表的瑕疵或斑点

entries.definition: marked or spoiled on the surface
entries.definitionCN: 有瑕疵的；被玷污的

entries.definition: one who spoils or stains something
entries.definitionCN: 损害或玷污某物的人（罕用）

entries.definition: having no fault or weakness at all
entries.definitionCN: 完美无瑕的

entries.definition: completely clean
entries.definitionCN: 一尘不染的

entries.definition: perfectly clean and without any stain
entries.definitionCN: 洁白无瑕的

normalIntro.en: Unblemished is a surface with the un- lid still on: nothing has ever left a mark.
normalIntro.cn: unblemished 是一个盖着 un- 这个「否定盖子」的表面：从来没有任何东西留下痕迹。

normal.en: Blemish means a mark, so unblemished means no mark.
normal.cn: blemish 意为痕迹，所以 unblemished 意为没有痕迹。

normal.en: The -ed ending shows it describes the thing that has the quality.
normal.cn: 结尾 -ed 表明它形容具有这种性质的事物。

normal.en: People say an unblemished record, an unblemished career, an unblemished skin.
normal.cn: 常见搭配有清白无瑕的记录、毫无瑕疵的生涯、光洁的皮肤。

normal.en: The word is formal and slightly literary, used in praise rather than complaint.
normal.cn: 这个词偏正式、略带书面色彩，用于赞美而非抱怨。

normal.en: Its opposite is blemished, not unblemish, because the adjective keeps the participle shape.
normal.cn: 它的反义形式是 blemished，而不是 unblemish，因为形容词保留了分词形状。

abstract.en: See an apple polished to a sheen with not one scratch.
abstract.cn: 想象一只被擦得发亮的苹果，连一道划痕也没有。

abstract.en: See a page of a record book with no entries crossed out.
abstract.cn: 想象一页记录本，上面没有任何条目被划掉。

abstract.en: See a white wall that has never been touched by a hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一面从未被人触碰过的白墙。

examples.en: She chose an unblemished apple from the box.
examples.cn: 她从箱子里挑了一只光滑无损的苹果。

examples.en: The hotel kept its unblemished reputation for service.
examples.cn: 酒店保持了服务方面毫无污点的名声。

examples.en: The team finished the season with an unblemished record.
examples.cn: 球队以全胜无瑕的战绩结束了赛季。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安布莱米须特」——想象一块「安」静光「布」，上面「莱米须」般细小的须痕都被「特」别擦得干干净净，所以一点瑕疵也没有；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古英语 blemischen（损坏表面）← 一般认为源自古法语 ble(s)mir（使变苍白，此源有一定争议）→ 名词 blemish（瑕疵）→ 分词 blemished → un- + blemished → unblemished（无瑕疵的）。

sensesIntro.en: Unblemished begins with a clean surface, moves to a clean record, extends to moral purity, and ends as praise for anything perfect.
sensesIntro.cn: unblemished 从洁净的表面说起，再指清白的记录，扩展到道德纯洁，最后成为对完美事物的赞语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an apple with not one scratch on its skin.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只表皮上连一道划痕都没有的苹果。

branches.en: A clean physical surface is the first and most literal sense.
branches.cn: 洁净的表面是第一个、也最字面的义项。

branches.en: A record treated as a surface is the second sense.
branches.cn: 把记录当成表面来看，是第二个义项。

branches.en: Purity of name is the moral sense.
branches.cn: 名誉的纯洁，是道德层面的义项。

branches.en: Praise for flawless quality generalises the idea.
branches.cn: 对毫无瑕疵的赞美，是这一概念的泛化。

branches.en: Both a clean record and a clean name deny blame.
branches.cn: 清白的记录与清白的名声都否定了过错。

intro.en: Unblemished is a compound of the negative prefix un- and the participle blemished, built on the noun blemish.
intro.cn: unblemished 由否定前缀 un- 与分词 blemished 组合而成，而 blemished 又建立在名词 blemish 之上。

latinIntro.en: English un- has a distant Indo-European relative in Latin in- and Old French mes-, both of which also mark negation or badness.
latinIntro.cn: 英语前缀 un- 与拉丁语否定前缀 in-、古法语表示「坏」的前缀 mes- 都是同源远亲。

items.example: The prefix un- turns blemished into unblemished.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 把 blemished 变成 unblemished。

items.meaning: a mark that spoils a surface
items.example: A blemish can be small but visible.
items.exampleCN: 瑕疵可以很小，却看得见。

items.example: To blemish is to leave a mark.
items.exampleCN: blemish 作动词表示留下痕迹。

items.meaningCN: 构成动词或形容词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ish shapes blemish.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ish 构成了 blemish 的形状。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms blemished.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 blemished。

items.example: Blemished fruit is sold at a lower price.
items.exampleCN: 带瑕疵的水果会便宜出售。

items.example: The suffix -less forms related words such as flawless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 flawless 等同族词。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms unblemishedness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 unblemishedness。

latinEntries.example: Latin in- is a distant relative of English un-.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 in- 与英语 un- 同源远亲。

latinEntries.example: Macula lies behind English immaculate and maculate.
latinEntries.exampleCN: macula 是英语 immaculate 与 maculate 的词源。

definition_zh: 不关心的；不在意的；漠不关心的；无忧无虑的
definition_en: not worried about something, or not interested enough in it to care what happens
core_image: 别人在旁边着急跺脚，一个人却低头翻书，连头都不抬
scene: 办公室里大家都在为截止日期忙碌，一位同事却端着咖啡慢悠悠地翻杂志，仿佛这一切与他无关。He seemed quite unconcerned about the approaching deadline.
sceneCN: 这里 unconcerned 是「不关心的、不在意的」（第 1 个义项：对可能担心的事毫不在意）；句意：他似乎对即将到来的截止日期毫不在意。

pos.zh: 不关心的；漠不关心的；无忧无虑的

forms.label: 作表语（接 about 或 with）

derivatives.zh: 漠不关心；无忧无虑
漠不关心地；满不在乎地
担心的；关心的
关心；忧虑；利害关系
漠然；无动于衷

senses.title: Not worried about something
senses.definition: not worried or anxious about something that worries other people
senses.definitionCN: 对别人会担心的事并不担心或焦虑
senses.example: She remained unconcerned about the exam results.
senses.exampleCN: 她对考试成绩仍然毫不在意。
senses.why: The un- prefix cancels the verb concern, meaning to make someone anxious, so the word literally means not troubled by worry.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 抵消了动词 concern（使人忧虑）的力量，所以这个词字面上就是「没有被忧虑纠缠」。

senses.title: Not interested in what matters
senses.definition: not showing interest in something that deserves attention
senses.definitionCN: 对值得关注的事情不表现出兴趣
senses.example: The manager seemed unconcerned with the safety complaints.
senses.exampleCN: 经理似乎对安全投诉漠不关心。
senses.why: When the absent worry is one that other people think you owe, the word turns from calm into a criticism of coldness.
senses.whyCN: 当缺席的忧虑是旁人认为你本应有的，这个词就从「沉着」变成了对冷淡的批评。

senses.title: Not involved in something
senses.titleCN: 与……无关的；不牵涉其中的
senses.definition: having no part in a situation or no connection with a matter
senses.definitionCN: 与某种情况没有关系或不参与其中
senses.example: The judges were unconcerned in the dispute between the two firms.
senses.exampleCN: 法官们并未牵涉两家公司之间的争端。
senses.why: Concern also names a relationship or involvement, so denying concern denies any stake in the matter.
senses.whyCN: concern 也指关系或牵涉，所以否定 concern 就是否认与该事有任何利害关系。

senses.title: Carefree and easy
senses.titleCN: 无忧无虑的；轻松自在的
senses.definition: relaxed and happy because nothing seems to trouble you
senses.definitionCN: 因没有什么困扰而轻松愉快
senses.example: The children looked unconcerned as they played by the river.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在河边玩耍，看起来无忧无虑。
senses.why: If none of the usual worries are present, the result is a natural lightness, and the word takes on a positive tone.
senses.whyCN: 如果常见的烦恼都不在场，结果自然是一种轻盈自在，这个词因此带上了正面色彩。

intro.en: Unconcerned is the negative of concerned, built on the verb concern, which came into English through French from Latin.
intro.cn: unconcerned 是 concerned 的否定形式，其基础动词 concern 经法语进入英语，源头是拉丁语。

items.en: Concernere means to sift together or to unite.
items.cn: 拉丁语 concernere 意为一起筛、混合并合为一体。

items.en: The prefix con- means together and cernere means to sift or separate.
items.cn: 前缀 con- 意为「一起」，cernere 意为「筛、分开」。

items.en: Concerner carries the idea of relating to or touching on a matter.
items.cn: 古法语 concerner 带来「涉及、关系到某事」的意思。

items.en: Concernen appears meaning to be of importance to someone.
items.cn: 中古英语 concernen 出现，意为「对某人重要、与某人有关」。

items.en: The adjective unconcerned is recorded meaning not troubled or not involved.
items.cn: 形容词 unconcerned 见于记载，意为不忧虑、不牵涉。

note.en: Unconcerned is the mirror of concerned, close to indifference on one side and light hearted freedom on the other.
note.cn: unconcerned 是 concerned 的镜像，一边靠近「漠然」，另一边靠近「轻松自在」。

entries.definition: worried or involved
entries.definitionCN: 担忧的；有关的

entries.definition: lack of worry or interest
entries.definitionCN: 漠不关心；无忧无虑

entries.definition: in a calm and careless way
entries.definitionCN: 满不在乎地

entries.definition: not interested and not caring
entries.definitionCN: 漠不关心的

entries.definition: not emotionally involved
entries.definitionCN: 超然的；置身事外的

entries.definition: showing no interest or energy
entries.definitionCN: 无动于衷的；麻木的

normalIntro.en: Unconcerned is a knot with no string: con- ties people together, and un- leaves the knot undone.
normalIntro.cn: unconcerned 是一个没有绳子的结：con- 把人系在一起，un- 则让这个结根本没打上。

normal.en: Concern is built from con- together and cernere to sift, so caring first means getting mixed up with things.
normal.cn: concern 由「一起」的 con- 与「筛、分选」的 cernere 构成，关心最初就是与事物搅在一起。

normal.en: Be unconcerned about a risk states calm, not necessarily coldness.
normal.cn: be unconcerned about 某风险说的大多是沉着，未必是冷淡。

normal.en: Reporters often write that a witness seemed unconcerned by the noise.
normal.cn: 记者常写某证人似乎对嘈杂声无动于衷。

normal.en: The noun form is unconcern, as in viewed the mess with unconcern.
normal.cn: 名词形式是 unconcern，例如「带着漠然看着这一片狼藉」。

normal.en: The word often carries judgement, so use indifferent when you want a neutral tone.
normal.cn: 这个词常带评价色彩，想中性表达时可用 indifferent。

abstract.en: See a person calmly reading while everyone else runs late.
abstract.cn: 想象大家都在赶时间，一个人却悠闲地看书。

abstract.en: See a child sleeping through a loud storm.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子在响亮的雷暴里安然熟睡。

abstract.en: See a colleague looking out of the window during a crisis.
abstract.cn: 想象危机当中一位同事望着窗外。

examples.en: He seemed unconcerned about the approaching deadline.
examples.cn: 他似乎对即将到来的截止日期毫不在意。

examples.en: The children were unconcerned as the wind picked up.
examples.cn: 风渐渐变大，孩子们却无忧无虑。

examples.en: She looked unconcerned by the criticism.
examples.cn: 面对批评，她显得毫不在意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安肯舍恩」——「安」心得很，肯把恩情都「舍」掉，也就是什么都不放在心上；这只是一种谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 con-（一起）+ cernere（筛、分开）→ concernere（混合、合为一体）→ 古法语 concerner（涉及、关系到）→ 英语 concern（关心；忧虑）→ concerned（关心的）→ un- + concerned → unconcerned。核心义「没有被牵系」。

sensesIntro.en: Unconcerned starts as freedom from worry, drifts into a criticism of coldness, marks a lack of involvement, and can finally sound light hearted.
sensesIntro.cn: unconcerned 先从「不担心」说起，滑向对冷淡的批评，再指不牵涉其中，最后可以听来轻松愉快。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person calmly reading while everyone around is hurrying.
core.cn: 核心意象：周围人都在赶时间，只有一个人悠闲地看书。

branches.en: Absence of worry is the first sense.
branches.cn: 不担心是第一个义项。

branches.en: Absence of proper care is the critical sense.
branches.cn: 该有的关心缺失，是带批评意味的义项。

branches.en: Absence of involvement is the relationship sense.
branches.cn: 不牵涉其中，是关系层面的义项。

branches.en: A carefree mood is the positive sense.
branches.cn: 无忧无虑的心境，是正面义项。

branches.en: Both the calm and the carefree feelings grow from the absence of worry.
branches.cn: 沉着与轻松两种感受都来自忧虑的缺席。

intro.en: Unconcerned is a three part word: un- denies, con- joins, and the root cern- adds the idea of sifting.
intro.cn: unconcerned 由三部分组成：un- 表示否定，con- 表示一起，词根 cern- 带来「筛、分选」的含义。

latinIntro.en: Latin cernere means to sift, distinguish, or decide, and concernere mixes things by sifting them together.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cernere 意为筛、分辨、决定，concernere 则意为把这些东西筛到一起、混为一体。

items.example: The prefix un- turns concerned into unconcerned.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 把 concerned 变成 unconcerned。

items.example: The prefix con- is a shortening of Latin com-.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 con- 是拉丁语 com- 的缩短形式。

items.example: The root cern- appears in discern and secret.
items.exampleCN: 词根 cern- 也见于 discern 与 secret。

items.example: To concern someone is to matter to them.
items.exampleCN: concern 某人就是对某人重要。

items.meaning: worry, or a matter of interest
items.example: The noun concern names both a worry and a business.
items.exampleCN: 名词 concern 既指忧虑，也指事务。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms concerned.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 concerned。

definition_zh: 不可征服的；无法战胜的；克制不住的
definition_en: impossible to defeat, overcome, or bring under control
core_image: 一支军队攻到城墙下，撞了又撞，墙始终立着
scene: 历史课上讲到一座小城，敌军围了整整一个冬天也没能攻进去。In the history lesson we read about a small town that stayed unconquerable through a whole winter of siege.
sceneCN: 这里 unconquerable 是「无法攻克、不可征服」（第 1 个义项：军事上攻不下来）；句意：历史课上我们读到一座小城，在整整一个冬天的围攻中始终无法被攻克。

pos.zh: 不可征服的；无法战胜的；克制不住的

derivatives.zh: 源于拉丁语 conquaerere（追寻、争取），词义演变为「征服」；加上 un- 与 -able 后成为「无法被征服的」
conquer 加 -able（可被……的），义为「可以被征服的」
conquer 加 -or（做某事的人或物），义为「征服者」
与 conquer 同源的拉丁语 -quest 名词形式，义为「征服；攻占」
unconquerable 加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不可征服地」

senses.title: That cannot be taken by force
senses.titleCN: 攻不下的；无法被占领的
senses.definition: said of a city, army, or people that cannot be beaten or captured by force
senses.definitionCN: 形容城池、军队或人群无法被武力击败或攻占
senses.example: The castle proved unconquerable to wave after wave of attackers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城堡在一波又一波的进攻面前难以攻下。
senses.why: The Latin verb conquaerere means to seek out and take into hand, so what is taken can be conquered; un- before an adjective denies exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 conquaerere 意为「追寻并拿到手里」，凡是被拿下的东西就是被征服了；形容词前的否定前缀 un- 正好把这一动作否定掉，于是就成了「拿不下来」。

senses.title: Cannot be overcome in a struggle
senses.titleCN: 无法战胜的；难以对付的
senses.definition: so strong or difficult that no effort or opposition can defeat it
senses.definitionCN: 极其强大或艰难，任何努力或对抗都无法将其击败
senses.example: Their defence looked unconquerable in the second half.
senses.exampleCN: 下半场他们的防线看起来无法攻破。
senses.why: From a walled city the sense widens: conquest means winning a contest of any kind, so anything that resists every attempt to beat it is unconquerable.
senses.whyCN: 从有城墙的城池向外延伸：conquer 的意思是赢得任何形式的较量，所以凡是如何努力都打不败的对象，都可以说 unconquerable。

senses.title: That cannot be put down
senses.titleCN: 克制不住的；难以压制的
senses.definition: said of a feeling, desire, or habit that no one can control or get rid of
senses.definitionCN: 形容情感、欲望或习惯无法被控制或消除
senses.example: He felt an unconquerable urge to laugh at the worst moment.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最糟的时刻感到一股克制不住的大笑冲动。
senses.why: Conquering also means mastering oneself; a feeling that refuses to be mastered borrows the same word, as if the emotion had an army of its own.
senses.whyCN: 征服也指战胜自己；一种拒绝被驯服的情绪借用了同一个词，仿佛这种情绪自己带着一支军队。

senses.title: Unbeatable in the abstract
senses.definition: said of a problem, obstacle, or flaw that no solution appears to remove
senses.definitionCN: 形容问题、障碍或缺陷似乎没有解决办法可以消除
senses.example: The village struggled with an unconquerable shortage of water.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子一直为无法解决的缺水问题发愁。
senses.why: A siege can be military, economic, or social; once the word describes any resistance, even a problem is pictured as a fortress no plan can storm.
senses.whyCN: 围攻可以是军事的、经济的或社会的；一旦这个词用来形容任何「抵抗」，连问题也会被想象成一座任何方案都攻不进去的堡垒。

senses.title: Not to be overcome by hardship
senses.definition: describing a person or spirit that survives defeat, hardship, or loss without giving in
senses.definitionCN: 形容人或精神在失败、困苦或失去之后依然不肯低头
senses.example: Her unconquerable optimism kept the whole team going.
senses.exampleCN: 她那不屈不挠的乐观精神让整个队伍坚持了下来。
senses.why: The oldest epic stories turn the military sense inward: the hero is defeated yet his spirit is never taken, so the adjective moves from walls to will.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的史诗把军事含义转向内心：英雄会被击倒，但他的精神永远不会被夺走，于是这个词从城墙挪到了意志上。

senses.title: Not settled or fully known
senses.titleCN: 未被彻底摸清的；尚无定论的
senses.definition: not yet fully explored, understood, or brought under human control
senses.definitionCN: 尚未被完全探索、理解或置于人的掌控之下
senses.example: The furthest mountains remained unconquerable to early map makers.
senses.exampleCN: 对早期的制图者来说，最远的群山仍然是无法探明的。
senses.why: To conquer a land first meant to walk all of it; ground never surveyed is therefore ground never conquered, and the word survives as a mild hyperbole.
senses.whyCN: 征服一块土地最初意味着走遍它；从未勘测过的土地就是从未被征服的土地，这个词便以温和的夸张方式延续下来。

senses.title: Literary and archaic praise
senses.definition: in older and literary English, a high-flown way of saying utterly unbeatable
senses.definitionCN: 在较古老的文学英语中，用来夸张地表达「完全无敌」
senses.example: The bard sang of an unconquerable knight no blade could touch.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人歌唱一位任何刀剑都伤不到的、无人能敌的骑士。
senses.why: This elevated use comes straight from the strong verb: poets kept the word for the finest warrior in the tale, and it has stayed in verse ever since.
senses.whyCN: 这种高雅的用法直接来自那个强有力的动词：诗人一直用它称呼故事里最出色的武士，此后它便留在诗歌里。

intro.en: Unconquerable is Latin com-, with, plus quaerere, to seek, through the strong verb conquaerere, to seek out and obtain, with an English negative prefix and a possibility suffix.
intro.cn: unconquerable 由拉丁语前缀 com-（一起）与 quaerere（寻找）合成conquaerere（追寻并取得），再经古法语进入英语，加上否定前缀 un- 与表「能够」的后缀 -able 而成。

items.en: The verb quaerere means to seek, question, or strive for.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 quaerere 意为寻找、探究、努力求得。

items.en: Conquaerere combines com- with quaerere: to seek something out and get it.
items.cn: conquaerere 由 com- 与 quaerere 合成，义为「寻找并取得」。

items.en: Old French conquere picks up the verb with the meaning to win by force.
items.cn: 古法语 conquere 接过这个动词，含义变成「靠武力赢得」。

items.en: Middle English takes over conquer, and later French forms carry the verb forward.
items.cn: 中古英语接过 conquer 这一形式，后来的法语形式继续把这个动词往前推。

items.en: The modern form is recorded from the fifteenth century on: a Latin verb, a French reflex, and an English suffix folded into one long adjective.
items.cn: 现代形式自十五世纪起见于书面：一个拉丁动词、一个法语反射形、一个英语后缀，被压进一个长长的形容词里。

note.en: Unconquerable is the adjective of the conquest family, with unbeatable and invincible as its nearest neighbours in meaning.
note.cn: unconquerable 属于「征服」词族，意义上的近邻是 unbeatable 与 invincible。

normalIntro.en: Build the word in three pieces: un-, conquer, and -able, and let the picture of a stubborn fortress do the rest.
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆成三段：un-、conquer 与 -able，再用一座顽固堡垒的画面托住它。

normal.en: Un- denies, conquer claims, and -able allows, so the whole word means cannot be claimed.
normal.cn: un- 表示否定，conquer 是「征服」，-able 表「能够」，合起来就是「不能被拿下」。

normal.en: Conquer shifts meaning from seeking to winning, and qu- words often hint at seeking.
normal.cn: conquer 的词义从「寻找」漂移到「赢得」，而带 qu- 的词常留有「寻」的味道。

normal.en: The suffixes un- and -able stack neatly, so compare conquerable for the opposite idea.
normal.cn: 前缀 un- 与后缀 -able 整齐叠加，对比 conquerable 即可看到相反的意思。

normal.en: A fixed phrase to keep is an unconquerable spirit, which is praise rather than a military report.
normal.cn: 记住固定说法 an unconquerable spirit，它是在赞美，而不是军事报告。

normal.en: Note that conqueror has an -or for the person, while conquest names the act itself.
normal.cn: 注意 conqueror 用 -or 指人，而 conquest 指行为本身。

abstract.en: See a wall that shakes with every blow yet never falls.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙在每次撞击中颤动，却始终不倒。

abstract.en: Imagine a flag on the rampart that no enemy hand can pull down.
abstract.cn: 想象城头一面旗帜，任何敌手都扯不下来。

abstract.en: Picture a feeling like a wave that keeps surging back however often it is pushed away.
abstract.cn: 想象一种情绪像浪潮，被推开多少次就涌回多少次。

examples.en: The general told his troops that the fortress was unconquerable.
examples.cn: 将军告诉部队，这座要塞是无法攻克的。

examples.en: They faced an unconquerable tide of complaints from the public.
examples.cn: 他们面对一股无法遏制的公众抱怨浪潮。

examples.en: The book describes the sailors as unconquerable in the face of the storm.
examples.cn: 书中描述这些水手在风暴面前不屈不挠。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「刚可」——城墙刚可挡住一切，所以 un-conquer-able 就是「不会被征服」；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 com-（一起）+ quaerere（寻找）→ conquaerere（寻找并取得）→ 古法语 conquerre → 英语 conquer（征服）；加否定前缀 un-（不）与后缀 -able（能够被……的）构成 unconquerable，核心义「拿不下来」。

sensesIntro.en: Unconquerable starts with a fortress that will not fall, spreads to any contest no one can win, then turns inward to feelings that cannot be mastered and people who will not give in.
sensesIntro.cn: unconquerable 从攻不下的要塞出发，扩展到任何没有人能赢的较量，再转向内心：无法压制的情绪与不肯低头的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fortress that shakes under every blow but never falls.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座在每一下重击中都晃动、却从不倒塌的堡垒。

branches.en: The physical fortress and the lost contest share one refusal to be beaten.
branches.cn: 有形的堡垒与被夺走的胜利共享同一种「打不败」。

branches.en: An emotion becomes a little army that cannot be routed.
branches.cn: 情绪变成一支无法被击溃的小军队。

branches.en: A problem is pictured as a siege that no plan can lift.
branches.cn: 问题被想象成任何方案都解不开的围城。

branches.en: Hardship attacks the person, and the person simply will not surrender.
branches.cn: 困苦攻击着人，而人就是不肯投降。

branches.en: The words oldest layer keeps its literary and open-ended flavour in verse and maps.
branches.cn: 这个词最古老的层次在诗歌与地图里保留着文学与开放性的味道。

intro.en: Unconquerable is built from the Latin root quaer-, the Latin prefix com-, and the English affixes un- and -able.
intro.cn: unconquerable 由拉丁词根 quaer-、拉丁前缀 com- 以及英语词缀 un- 与 -able 构成。

latinIntro.en: The true Latin source is conquaerere, to seek out and obtain, alongside its noun forms, and its verb to seek.
latinIntro.cn: 真正的拉丁语来源是 conquaerere（追寻并取得），以及它的名词形式与表示「寻找」的动词。

items.example: Un- makes unconquerable negative.
items.exampleCN: un- 把 unconquerable 变成否定。

items.example: The quer root also appears in inquire and question.

items.example: The suffix -able turns a verb into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 把动词变作形容词。

items.example: Conquere reaches English through Old French.
items.exampleCN: conquere 经古法语进入英语。

items.example: Conquerable is the positive partner of this word.
items.exampleCN: conquerable 是本词的反向形态。

items.example: Conquest names the whole campaign.
items.exampleCN: conquest 指整场征服行动。

items.example: The suffix -or names the person.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 指做这件事的人。

items.example: The suffix -ly gives the adverb unconquerably.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成副词 unconquerably。
